why: Rennala NIGT and Malenia NIGT improve computation and communication complexity for distributed RL under homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous settings, supported by theory and experiments

topic: Few-function-evaluation image generation through damped-wave probability flows
why: The first-party abstract explicitly targets fast image generation, uses endpoint-only teacher-to-student distillation, and reports high-quality samples with very few function evaluations; this is a direct, high-value generation-acceleration contribution.

title: DistMLIP: A Distributed Inference Platform for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
topic: Zero-redundancy graph-parallel distributed inference for ML interatomic potentials
why: The official abstract directly targets scaling atomistic simulations by parallelizing ML interatomic-potential inference across devices with zero redundancy. This is a direct distributed-inference and scientific-compute efficiency contribution.

title: Distributionally Robust Linear Regression with Block Lewis Weights
topic: Block Lewis weights for robust regression
why: The algorithm obtains a (1+epsilon)-optimal solution with a stated reduced number of linear-system solves and improves on known interior-point methods in moderate-accuracy regimes. This is a direct algorithmic-complexity efficiency contribution

title: Divid: Disentangled Spatial-Temporal Modeling within LLMs for Temporally Grounded Video Understanding
topic: Spatial-temporal token efficiency for long-video LLM understanding
why: The official abstract identifies long visual-token sequences and context/computation cost as bottlenecks, then separates spatial and temporal processing. This directly targets long-video MLLM efficiency.

title: Do We Need All the Synthetic Data? Targeted Image Augmentation via Diffusion Models
topic: Targeted synthetic-data selection for compute-efficient image-model training
why: The official abstract directly addresses synthetic-data overhead, augments only 30–40% of examples instead of the usual 10–30× dataset expansion, and reports up to 2.8% generalization gains; this is a strong training-efficiency contribution.

title: DOPPLER: Dual-Policy Learning for Device Assignment in Asynchronous Dataflow Graphs
topic: Dataflow scheduling, device placement, ML workload execution efficiency
why: The official abstract optimizes operation selection and device placement in asynchronous dataflow execution, reports reduced execution time and improved sampling efficiency, and gives a substantial measured performance result. This is directly relevant to ML systems and compiler/runtime efficiency.

title: Dr.LLM: Dynamic Layer Routing in LLMs
why: The official abstract routes tokens through skip, execute, or repeat decisions and reports saving five layers per example with only 0.85 percent accuracy drop on broad OOD tasks. This is a direct adaptive-compute inference method.

title: Draft-based Approximate Inference for LLMs
topic: KV cache compression / sparse attention / prompt compression
why: Uses a small draft model to predict token/KV importance, introducing SpecKV, SpecPC and SpecKV-PC for more accurate approximate long-context inference.

title: DriftLite: Lightweight Drift Control for Inference-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models
why: The official abstract contrasts lightweight guidance with high-cost particle corrections and proposes a training-free, lightweight drift-control method. Retain as a direct inference-time compute-efficiency lead.

title: DRPO: Efficient Reasoning via Decoupled Reward Policy Optimization
topic: reducing reasoning-token and latency overhead in LLMs
why: The official abstract targets overthinking and redundant reasoning, and reports 77% shorter reasoning with only 1.1% accuracy loss on GSM8k for a 1.5B model. The decoupled reward objective directly optimizes reasoning efficiency while preserving correctness; promote strongly.

title: DSA: Efficient Inference For Video Generation Models via Distributed Sparse Attention
topic: distributed sparse attention for video generation inference
why: The official abstract reports sparse attention plus distributed inference/scheduling that reduces redundant computation, with 1.43x speedup over an existing distributed method and 10.79x over single-GPU inference.

title: DTP: Delta-Guided Two Stage Pruning for Mamba-based Multimodal Large Language Models
topic: Visual-token pruning for Mamba MLLM inference
why: The official abstract directly targets redundant visual tokens and prefill-dominated inference cost in Mamba MLLMs, using Mamba-specific importance scores for progressive pruning. This is a direct multimodal inference-efficiency method.

title: Dual-objective Language Models: Training Efficiency Without Overfitting
why: The official abstract directly targets training efficiency while controlling overfitting. This is a core efficient-ML training contribution rather than generic language-model quality work.

title: Dual-Solver: A Generalized ODE Solver for Diffusion Models with Dual Prediction
topic: Low-NFE diffusion sampling with learned generalized ODE solvers
why: The official abstract directly targets costly diffusion sampling and reports improved FID/CLIP quality in the low-NFE regime of 3–9 evaluations. This is a direct inference-efficiency contribution with a quantified low-step operating range.

title: DualMap: Enabling Both Cache Affinity and Load Balancing for Distributed LLM Serving
topic: dual-map scheduling for distributed LLM serving
why: The official abstract identifies the conflict between KV-cache affinity and load balancing, then introduces dual-mapping request scheduling to reduce TTFT and serving cost while maintaining balanced compute. This is a direct serving-system contribution.

title: DVD-Quant: Data-free Video Diffusion Transformers Quantization
topic: data-free PTQ for video diffusion transformers
why: The official abstract identifies Video DiT compute and memory demands and proposes data-free PTQ to accelerate deployment without computation-heavy calibration. This is a direct generation-model compression and inference-efficiency contribution.

title: Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models
why: The first-party abstract directly targets overthinking in reasoning LLMs and reports 19.1–80.1% shorter CoT with 0.3–5.0% accuracy gains across 11 models and 10 benchmarks, a concrete inference-efficiency improvement.

title: Dynamic Speculative Agent Planning
topic: Lossless speculative acceleration for LLM agents
why: The official abstract jointly optimizes agent latency and dollar cost and reports 30 percent lower total cost and up to 60 percent lower unnecessary cost without pre-deployment preparation. This directly targets efficient agent inference.

title: Dynamic-dLLM: Dynamic Cache-Budget and Adaptive Parallel Decoding for Training-Free Acceleration of Diffusion LLM
topic: diffusion LLM cache-budgeting and parallel decoding
why: The official abstract identifies dLLM inference complexity and the inability to reuse standard KV caches, then introduces training-free dynamic cache-budget allocation and adaptive parallel decoding based on token dynamics. This directly targets inference efficiency.

title: DynamicInfer: Runtime-Aware Sparse Offloading for LLMs Inference on a Consumer-Grade GPU
topic: runtime sparse offloading for consumer-GPU LLM inference
why: The official abstract introduces dynamic neuron scheduling, hierarchical caching, load-aware activation, and activation-aware prefetch to reduce memory/computation overhead and latency on heterogeneous consumer hardware. This directly targets edge/heterogeneous LLM inference.

title: EasyTune: Efficient Step-Aware Fine-Tuning for Diffusion-Based Motion Generation
topic: memory- and compute-efficient diffusion motion fine-tuning
why: The official abstract identifies inefficient coarse optimization and high memory use in reward-based motion-model fine-tuning, then proposes step-aware optimization. This is a direct training-efficiency contribution in the protected action-generation direction.

title: EchoGen: Generating Visual Echoes in Any Scene via Feed-Forward Subject-Driven Auto-Regressive Model
why: The official abstract explicitly contrasts costly per-subject fine-tuning and slow diffusion inference with rapid VAR sampling. EchoGen uses a feed-forward VAR foundation to provide subject-driven generation, directly targeting generation speed and adaptation cost.

title: Efficient Approximate Posterior Sampling with Annealed Langevin Monte Carlo
topic: efficient posterior sampling for score-based generative models
why: The official abstract directly studies efficient approximate posterior sampling for score-based models and motivates improvements over computationally costly existing sampling procedures. Retain as a strong sampling-efficiency method.

title: Efficient Discriminative Joint Encoders for Large Scale Vision-Language Reranking
why: The official abstract reports 50k image-text pairs per second and reduced online compute/storage through offline visual-token encoding, with retrieval performance matching prior art.

title: Efficient Learning on Large Graphs using a Densifying Regularity Lemma
why: The IBG low-rank graph representation and associated GNN reduce memory and computational complexity from edge-linear to node-linear while retaining competitive graph-task performance. This is a direct algorithmic efficiency contribution for large-graph learning.

title: Efficient Multimodal Spatial Reasoning via Dynamic and Asymmetric Routing
topic: Token and KV-cache reduction for multimodal reasoning
why: The official abstract reports average 40.37% FLOPs reduction and 46.07% KV-cache reduction while preserving or improving reasoning performance across seven benchmarks.

title: Efficient Prediction of Large Protein Complexes via Subunit-Guided Hierarchical Refinement
why: The official abstract reports about 25 GB or 40% peak-memory reduction on a 4000-token target and successful inference beyond 5000 tokens that OOM AlphaFold3, with higher success rates.

title: Efficient Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts with Theoretical Generalization Guarantees
why: ICLR 2026 direct MoE inference-compression work using expert-wise mixed precision guided by router-norm change and intra-neuron variance, reducing inference cost with negligible allocation overhead.

title: Efficient Regression-based Training of Normalizing Flows for Boltzmann Generators
topic: Efficient normalizing-flow training and scientific generative models
why: The official abstract identifies unstable and computationally challenging maximum-likelihood training and replaces it with a scalable regression objective. This is a direct training-efficiency and numerical-stability contribution for normalizing flows.

title: Efficient Resource-Constrained Training of Transformers via Subspace Optimization
topic: On-device transformer training and inference efficiency
why: WASI directly targets transformer backpropagation memory and reports up to 62 times lower memory, 2 times lower FLOPs, and roughly 1.4 times faster training and inference on Raspberry Pi 5 with comparable accuracy. This is a clear resource-constrained and edge-efficiency contribution.

title: Efficient Zero-shot Inpainting with Decoupled Diffusion Guidance
why: The official abstract identifies state-of-the-art zero-shot methods' reliance on multiple surrogate likelihood score functions and proposes decoupled guidance. This directly addresses the compute cost of diffusion inference.

title: Efficient-LVSM: Faster, Cheaper, and Better Large View Synthesis Model via Decoupled Co-Refinement Attention
topic: linear/decoupled attention for large view synthesis
why: The official abstract removes unnecessary quadratic attention through dual-stream decoupled co-refinement and reports 2x faster training convergence and 4.2x faster inference with improved PSNR. This is a direct generative-vision acceleration contribution.

title: Efficient-SAM2: Accelerating SAM2 with Object-Aware Visual Encoding and Memory Retrieval
topic: post-training sparse visual encoding and memory retrieval
why: The official abstract identifies real-time video-processing cost in SAM2 and introduces object-aware encoder sparsity plus selective memory retrieval as post-training acceleration. This is a direct vision inference optimization with transferable token/memory mechanisms.

title: Eliciting Numerical Predictive Distributions of LLMs Without Auto-Regression
topic: Non-autoregressive numerical prediction and uncertainty inference
why: The official abstract states that repeated autoregressive sampling for numerical predictive distributions is costly and slow, then investigates lightweight probes that recover statistical functionals directly from representations. This directly targets inference cost.

title: Eliminating VAE for Fast and High-Resolution Generative Detail Restoration
topic: Diffusion super-resolution latency and memory optimization
why: The official abstract profiles the VAE as a latency and memory bottleneck and removes it through pixel-space generation and staged distillation. This directly addresses slow inference and high-resolution memory limits.

title: Embedding-Based Context-Aware Reranker
why: EBCAR replaces costly large-pretrained-language-model reranking with a lightweight embedding-based framework while modeling cross-passage context. The official abstract reports both accuracy and efficiency advantages on ConTEB, directly targeting RAG inference cost.

title: Enabling True Global Perception in State Space Models for Visual Tasks
why: GSSM addresses expensive attention-based global modeling with a frequency-aware SSM design and linear-logarithmic complexity, then validates GMamba across detection and segmentation tasks. This is a direct architecture-level efficiency contribution.

title: Energy-Efficient Random Variate Generation via Compressed Lookup Tables
topic: Probabilistic ML sampling primitives, energy/time efficiency
why: The official abstract reports a compressed-lookup-table sampling method for arbitrary distributions with up to 40% time and 50% energy savings in C microbenchmarks. This is a directly measured efficiency improvement in a core probabilistic-ML primitive.

title: Energy-oriented Diffusion Bridge for Image Restoration with Foundational Diffusion Models
topic: Low-cost diffusion-bridge trajectories and image-restoration inference
why: The official abstract identifies high-cost diffusion-bridge trajectories and proposes shorter trajectories plus a single-step consistency mapping. It directly reduces sampling cost while retaining an adaptive quality-versus-generation trade-off.

title: Enhancing Vision Transformers for Object Detection via Context-Aware Token Selection and Packing
topic: Token pruning and efficient ViT detection
why: SPA dynamically selects informative tokens and packs variable-size token batches for GPU training and inference. The official abstract reports 10.9–24.9 percent lower computation with 0.5–2.7 AP gains, directly demonstrating efficient vision-transformer execution.

title: Ensembling Pruned Attention Heads For Uncertainty-Aware Efficient Transformers
topic: pruned-head ensembles for efficient uncertainty estimation
why: The official abstract identifies ensemble inference/memory costs and constructs a compact pruned-head transformer ensemble with inference speed close to a single network while retaining uncertainty quality. This is a direct inference-efficiency contribution.

title: Entropy-Based Block Pruning for Efficient Large Language Models
topic: LLM block pruning and deployment compression
why: The method uses representation entropy to identify redundant transformer blocks and reports model-size reduction while preserving accuracy. This is a direct LLM compression and deployment-efficiency contribution, even though the abstract does not quantify a serving speedup.

title: Entropy-Guided Dynamic Tokens for Graph-LLM Alignment in Molecular Understanding
why: The official abstract replaces fixed connector tokens with entropy-guided dynamic tokens and freezes the LLM backbone, enabling computationally efficient fine-tuning while improving molecular understanding. This is a direct parameter- and training-efficient multimodal method.

title: Entropy-Monitored Kernelized Token Distillation for Audio-Visual Compression
why: The official abstract reports a student using 94% fewer parameters than the teacher while retaining 96.9% event-recognition and 96.5% segmentation performance. This is a direct, quantified multimodal compression/distillation contribution.

title: Equilibrium Language Models
topic: LLM compression, pruning, KV-cache memory reduction, edge inference
why: The official abstract proposes replacing Transformer layer groups with a lightweight fixed-point network, learned pruning intervals, and a one-step KV cache to reduce edge memory while preserving accuracy. This is a direct inference compression and memory-efficiency contribution.

title: ERGO: Efficient High-Resolution Visual Understanding for Vision-Language Models
why: The official abstract uses reasoning-driven region selection to process only relevant full-resolution crops, reducing visual-token compute while improving accuracy over the original model and competitive methods.

title: Error Feedback for Muon and Friends
why: The official abstract presents a principled distributed optimizer with convergence guarantees and bidirectional compression, reporting up to 7x communication savings without accuracy degradation on NanoGPT. This is a direct, quantified distributed-training efficiency contribution.

title: ERTACache: Error Rectification and Timesteps Adjustment for Efficient Diffusion
topic: error-corrected feature caching for diffusion inference
why: The official abstract identifies cumulative feature-cache error and fixed-timestep amplification, then introduces residual profiling, adaptive intervals, and cache correction. This directly targets iterative diffusion inference latency while controlling quality loss.

title: EventFlash: Towards Efficient MLLMs for Event-Based Vision
topic: Sparse event-token processing for efficient multimodal inference
why: The official abstract proposes temporal token aggregation and sparse-density-guided attention and reports a 12.4x throughput improvement over EventFlash-Zero while maintaining comparable performance.

title: Evoking User Memory: Personalizing LLM via Recollection-Familiarity Adaptive Retrieval
topic: adaptive retrieval to reduce LLM context overhead
why: The official abstract avoids feeding full user history into prompts and outperforms full-context reasoning under fixed budget and latency constraints. This directly reduces personalized-LLM context cost.

title: Evolutionary Caching to Accelerate Your Off-the-Shelf Diffusion Model
topic: Calibration-driven caching schedules for diffusion inference
why: The official abstract reports a 2.58x inference speedup on PixArt-alpha versus the previous 2.35x state of the art, with improved COCO FID and no model-parameter changes.

title: Expert Merging: Model Merging with Unsupervised Expert Alignment and Importance-Guided Layer Chunking
topic: Training-light expert merging for efficient LLM/MLLM deployment
why: The official abstract merges multiple experts into a single model using a small set of label-free coefficients, avoiding joint training or serving many models. Its importance-guided chunking improves parameter efficiency and scalable deployment.

title: FACT: Fine-grained Across-variable Convolution for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
topic: Efficient multivariate forecasting via across-variable convolution
why: The official abstract reports a convolutional architecture that captures dynamic cross-variable interactions while significantly reducing training time and memory versus attention, with state-of-the-art accuracy on twelve datasets. This is a direct efficient-attention/forecasting contribution.

title: FALCON: Few-step Accurate Likelihoods for Continuous Flows
topic: Few-step continuous-flow sampling and generative inference efficiency
why: The official abstract identifies likelihood evaluation requiring thousands of function evaluations as a practical bottleneck and proposes accurate few-step likelihoods. This directly reduces expensive generative inference work rather than merely improving sample quality.

title: FARI: Robust One-Step Inversion for Watermarking in Diffusion Models
topic: One-step diffusion inversion for watermark verification
why: The official abstract identifies high-NFE inversion as the bottleneck and reports a one-step inversion that is faster and more robust than 50-step DDIM while enabling practical adversarial fine-tuning.

title: FARTrack: Fast Autoregressive Visual Tracking with High Performance
topic: Autoregressive visual tracking, token sparsification, resource-constrained inference
why: The official abstract targets slow visual-tracker inference on resource-constrained devices and introduces task-specific self-distillation plus inter-frame autoregressive sparsification. This is a direct model-inference efficiency method.

title: FASA: FREQUENCY-AWARE SPARSE ATTENTION
topic: frequency-aware token eviction for long-context KV cache
why: The official abstract identifies KV-cache memory growth and irreversible token-eviction errors, then introduces query-aware eviction using RoPE frequency-chunk sparsity. This directly targets long-context inference memory and attention efficiency.

title: Fast Catch-Up, Late Switching: Optimal Batch Size Scheduling via Functional Scaling Laws
topic: Data-efficient large-scale pretraining through late batch-size switching
why: The official abstract shows that deferring large batches to late training can reduce data consumption without sacrificing performance and validates the schedule across dense and MoE LLM pretraining up to 1.1B parameters and 1T tokens. This is a direct large-scale training-efficiency result.

title: Fast Proteome-Scale Protein Interaction Retrieval via Residue-Level Factorization
topic: Factorized attention and approximate retrieval for proteome-scale ML
why: The official abstract reduces proteome-wide PPI retrieval from months to minutes by encoding each protein once and replacing exhaustive scoring with ANN retrieval; it reports 5.7 minutes on A100 versus 4.9 GPU-months for the prior method. This is a direct, quantified efficient retrieval result.

title: Fast-dLLM v2: Efficient Block-Diffusion LLM
topic: diffusion LLM inference / block diffusion / hierarchical caching
why: ICLR 2026 Poster. Extends Fast-dLLM into an efficient block-diffusion LLM with hierarchical caching and block-wise generation; official NVlabs project/repository confirms the accepted ICLR 2026 system.

title: Fast-dLLM: Training-free Acceleration of Diffusion LLM by Enabling KV Cache and Parallel Decoding
topic: diffusion LLM inference / KV cache / parallel decoding
why: ICLR 2026 Poster. Training-free block-wise approximate KV cache plus confidence-aware parallel decoding; official project reports large throughput gains and practical diffusion-LLM acceleration.

title: Fastcar: Cache Attentive Replay for Fast Auto-Regressive Video Generation on the Edge
topic: Temporal MLP-output caching and FPGA acceleration for video generation
why: The official abstract reports more than 2.1x decoding speedup and higher edge energy efficiency through temporal replay and an FPGA accelerator.

title: Faster Vision Transformers with Adaptive Patches
topic: Adaptive visual tokenization for efficient ViT inference and training
why: The official abstract uses content-adaptive patch sizes to reduce input tokens and reports 40 to 50 percent higher throughput on ViT-L/H and up to 30 percent faster training and inference on dense visual tasks without performance loss.

title: FASTer: Toward Powerful and Efficient Autoregressive Vision–Language–Action Models with Learnable Action Tokenizer and Block-wise Decoding
topic: compressed action tokenization and blockwise VLA decoding
why: The official abstract identifies the reconstruction/efficiency trade-off in VLA action tokenization and introduces a high-compression learnable tokenizer with blockwise autoregressive decoding and a lightweight action expert, reporting faster inference on simulation and real-world tasks. This is a direct protected Physical-AI serving contribution.

title: FastFlow: Accelerating The Generative Flow Matching Models with Bandit Inference
topic: adaptive bandit inference for flow matching
why: The official abstract identifies sequential denoising latency and proposes plug-and-play adaptive inference that approximates low-impact velocity steps without full model execution. This directly accelerates image/video flow generation.

title: FastGRPO: Accelerating Policy Optimization via Concurrency-aware Speculative Decoding and Online Draft Learning
topic: speculative decoding for LLM reinforcement-learning training
why: The official abstract identifies autoregressive response generation as the GRPO training bottleneck and introduces concurrency-aware speculative decoding plus online draft learning. This directly accelerates LLM training/inference generation.

title: FAST‑DIPS: Adjoint‑Free Analytic Steps and Hard‑Constrained Likelihood Correction for Diffusion‑Prior Inverse Problems
topic: Adjoint-free acceleration for diffusion-prior inverse problems
why: The official abstract explicitly replaces costly adjoint computations with analytic steps in a diffusion-prior inverse-problem workflow. This is a concrete algorithmic efficiency contribution for diffusion-based computation.

title: FideDiff: Efficient Diffusion Model for High-Fidelity Image Motion Deblurring
why: The official abstract identifies prohibitive diffusion inference time and introduces a one-step consistency-style deblurring model. This is a direct reduction in generative inference steps while retaining restoration quality.

title: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models via Intermediate Distribution Shaping
topic: Lower-FLOP diffusion fine-tuning through intermediate distribution shaping
why: The official abstract introduces distribution shaping and inverse-noise correction for pretrained diffusion/flow models and explicitly reports improved FID at lower FLOPs per image. This is a direct, quantified compute-efficiency contribution to generative-model fine-tuning.

title: Fine-tuning Quantized Neural Networks with Zeroth-order Optimization
why: The official abstract reports over 18x total-memory reduction versus 16-bit full-parameter tuning and enables Llama-2-13B fine-tuning on a single 24 GB GPU.

title: FLARE: Fully Integration of Vision-Language Representations for Deep Cross-Modal Understanding
why: The official abstract reports that a 3B FLARE model surpasses 8B baselines using only 630 vision tokens and achieves superior performance with minimal computational cost. This is a direct efficient VLM architecture result.

title: Flash-Mono: Feed-Forward Accelerated Gaussian Splatting Monocular SLAM
why: The official abstract reports bypassing per-frame optimization with a recurrent feed-forward frontend and achieving 10x speedup while retaining high-quality rendering; this is directly relevant to Physical AI.

title: Flash-Searcher: Fast and Effective Web Agents via DAG-Based Parallel Execution
topic: parallel DAG execution for lower agent latency
why: The first-party abstract replaces sequential tool execution with dependency-aware parallel DAGs and reports up to 35% fewer agent execution steps alongside strong benchmark results. This is direct agent-runtime efficiency.

title: FlashDLM: Accelerating Diffusion Language Model Inference via Efficient KV Caching and Guided Diffusion
topic: diffusion language model inference / KV caching / guided diffusion / decoding acceleration
why: ICLR 2026 poster. FlashDLM combines FreeCache KV approximation reuse with guided diffusion for diffusion-language-model inference; the paper reports 12.14x average end-to-end speedup with negligible accuracy degradation.

title: FlashVID: Efficient Video Large Language Models via Training-free Tree-based Spatiotemporal Token Merging
topic: Training-free spatiotemporal token merging for video MLLMs
why: The official abstract reports extending video-frame input by 10x for Qwen2.5-VL under the same computational budget and improving performance by 8.6% relative.

title: FlashWorld: High-quality 3D Scene Generation within Seconds
topic: Fast 3D scene generation, video diffusion, Gaussian scene representations
why: The official abstract reports 3D scene generation in seconds and roughly 10–100x faster generation than prior work, while directly producing 3D Gaussian representations. This is a concrete generative-inference latency reduction.

title: Flatter Tokens are More Valuable for Speculative Draft Model Training
why: SFDD filters speculative-draft training data using target-token predictive flatness and reports over 2 times training speedup with only 50 percent of data while keeping inference speedup within 4 percent of the full-data baseline. This directly improves speculative-decoding training efficiency.

title: FlexiCodec: A Dynamic Neural Audio Codec for Low Frame Rates
why: FlexiCodec adaptively merges semantically similar audio frames and exposes controllable 3–12.5 Hz frame rates, directly shortening speech-language-model sequences to reduce computational cost while preserving semantic and reconstruction quality. This is a concrete multimodal efficiency method.

title: FlexLinearAttention: Compiling a Unified Abstraction into Scalable Kernels for Linear Attention
topic: domain-specific compiler and scalable kernels for linear attention
why: The official abstract identifies the lack of hardware-efficient and distributed support for linear attention and introduces a DSL/compiler that generates optimized scalable kernels from high-level code. This directly targets GPU kernel/compiler and long-context efficiency.

title: FLoC: Facility Location-Based Efficient Visual Token Compression for Long Video Understanding
topic: facility-location visual token compression for video LLMs
why: The official abstract targets the dominant visual-token scalability bottleneck in long-video LMMs and selects a compact, representative subset under a token budget using lazy greedy facility-location optimization. It is training-free, model-agnostic, and reports robust benchmark performance and processing-efficiency gains; promote strongly.

title: Flow Caching for Autoregressive Video Generation
topic: Autoregressive video generation, flow reuse/cache, long-horizon inference
why: The official abstract identifies sequential video-chunk generation as slow and proposes chunk-specific flow-cache policies to avoid redundant recomputation. This is a direct inference-cache optimization for long video generation.

title: Flow Map Learning Via Non-Gradient Vector Flow
topic: Flow-map learning without expensive iterative differentiation
why: The official abstract identifies sampling integration overhead and expensive differentiation through model iteration, then introduces SGFlow to bypass those costs while learning flow maps. It reports a favorable FID-to-step-count relationship, making this a direct flow-generation efficiency contribution.

title: Flow-Based Single-Step Completion for Efficient and Expressive Policy Learning
topic: single-step flow policy inference for embodied/action generation
why: The official abstract identifies iterative flow sampling as a high inference-cost bottleneck and proposes one-shot action generation for offline, offline-to-online, and online RL. This is directly relevant to protected Physical-AI action inference.

title: Flow2GAN: Hybrid Flow Matching and GAN with Multi-Resolution Network for Few-step High-Fidelity Audio Generation
topic: Few-step audio generation, flow matching, GAN inference
why: The official abstract identifies multi-step flow-matching inference as computationally costly and combines flow training with GAN fine-tuning for efficient few-step audio generation. This is a direct generative-inference compute reduction.

title: FlowBind: Efficient Any-to-Any Generation with Bidirectional Flows
why: The first-party abstract reports comparable quality with up to 6x fewer parameters and 10x faster training by factorizing cross-modal interactions into shared latent flows. This is direct generation efficiency.

title: FlowCast: Trajectory Forecasting for Scalable Zero-Cost Speculative Flow Matching
topic: Speculative flow matching, generative inference acceleration
why: The official abstract directly identifies slow multi-step flow-matching inference and proposes training-free speculative velocity extrapolation with no additional cost, accepting predictions under an error threshold. This is a direct inference-acceleration method.

title: Fly-CL: A Fly-Inspired Framework for Enhancing Efficient Decorrelation and Reduced Training Time in Pre-trained Model-based Continual Representation Learning
topic: reduced training time for continual representation learning
why: The official abstract directly targets computationally prohibitive similarity matching and reports substantially reduced training time with comparable or better performance. Its low-time-complexity decorrelation method is a strong training-efficiency contribution.

title: Forest-Based Graph Learning for Semi-Supervised Node Classification
why: FGL replaces costly stacked-layer or global-attention long-range propagation with a forest paradigm and a linear-time tree aggregator realizing quadratic node-pair interactions. The abstract reports comparable node-classification results while remaining efficient, a direct graph-learning algorithmic efficiency contribution.

title: Forward-Learned Discrete Diffusion: Learning how to noise to denoise faster
topic: Discrete diffusion, learned noising, few-step generation
why: The official abstract explicitly targets long and expensive discrete-diffusion sampling and learns the forward noising process to reduce the gap to the target distribution and enable few-step generation. This is direct sampling-efficiency evidence.

title: FragFM: Hierarchical Framework for Efficient Molecule Generation via Fragment-Level Discrete Flow Matching
topic: Efficient molecular graph generation, hierarchical discrete flow matching
why: The official abstract explicitly proposes a coarse-to-fine fragment-level flow-matching framework to make molecular generation more efficient and scalable. It directly reduces the generation search space, though its full quantitative trade-offs remain to be checked.

title: FrameThinker: Learning to Think with Long Videos via Multi-Turn Frame Spotlighting
topic: Long-video reasoning, adaptive frame selection, multimodal inference efficiency
why: The official abstract identifies uniform frame sampling and static reasoning as inefficient for long-video tasks and introduces iterative frame interrogation/spotlighting. This directly targets the visual-token and reasoning-work bottleneck in long-video inference.

title: FreeKV: Boosting KV Cache Retrieval for Efficient LLM Inference
topic: KV cache retrieval / CPU-GPU hybrid memory / long-context inference
why: ICLR 2026 Poster. Algorithm-system co-design with speculative retrieval, fine-grained correction, hybrid CPU/GPU layouts and double-buffered streamed recall; reports up to 13x speedup over prior KV retrieval methods.

title: FreqKV: Key-Value Compression in Frequency Domain for Context Window Extension
why: FreqKV directly compresses the growing LLM KV cache in the frequency domain and extends LLaMA-2-7B from 8K training context to 256K while maintaining stable perplexity. It is a clear cache/memory efficiency and long-context serving contribution.

title: From Large to Small: Transferring CUDA Optimization Expertise via Reasoning Graph
topic: GPU kernel optimization and small-model CUDA code generation
why: The first-party abstract directly targets CUDA optimization and reports 2.33x average speedup on CUDAEval and ParEval. Its training-free reasoning-graph search transfers optimization expertise to small code models without excessive local compute, making it a core GPU-kernel/DSL efficiency contribution.

title: From Parameters to Behaviors: Unsupervised Compression of the Policy Space
topic: low-dimensional policy-space compression for sample-efficient RL
why: The official abstract compresses policy parameterizations by up to five orders of magnitude while retaining most behavior and enabling latent-space policy-gradient adaptation. This directly targets DRL sample inefficiency.

title: From Predictors to Samplers via the Training Trajectory
topic: Compute-light sampling using coarse-to-fine training checkpoints
why: The official abstract presents a compute-light alternative to diffusion sampling, reuses existing training checkpoints without additional compute, and reports a near-linear rather than exponential bottleneck in a Boolean setting. This is a direct sampling-compute contribution.

title: From Text to Talk: Audio-Language Model Needs Non-Autoregressive Joint Training
topic: Parallel non-autoregressive audio generation for multimodal inference
why: The official abstract replaces autoregressive audio generation with block-wise diffusion that synthesizes audio in parallel within a unified audio-text model. This directly targets sequential decoding overhead in multimodal serving.

title: From Tokens to Nodes: Semantic-Guided Motion Control for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting
why: The method uses motion-adaptive compression to allocate control points to dynamic regions and suppress static-background redundancy, replacing MLP deformation fields with spline trajectories. The official abstract reports improved reconstruction quality and efficiency, directly relevant to efficient 3D scene/world modeling.

title: From Verifiable Dot to Reward Chain: Harnessing Verifiable Reference-based Rewards for Reinforcement Learning of Open-ended Generation
topic: Data-efficient reinforcement learning for open-ended LLM generation
why: The official abstract reports that reference-based reward chains substantially outperform SFT trained with ten times more data while improving generalization and diversity. This is a direct training-data and alignment-efficiency contribution.

title: FROST: Filtering Reasoning Outliers with Attention for Efficient Reasoning
why: The official abstract describes attention-guided pruning of uncritical reasoning paths and reports a 69.68% average token reduction with a 26.70% accuracy improvement over the base model.

title: FrugalRAG: Less is More in RL Finetuning for Multi-hop Question Answering
why: FrugalRAG adaptively prunes retrieval depth by question difficulty and directly rewards correctness with frugality. The official abstract reports nearly halved retrieval cost with competitive accuracy and strong zero-shot generalization, making it a direct efficient reasoning/RAG systems contribution.

title: FS-DFM: Fast and Accurate Long Text Generation with Few-Step Diffusion Language Models
topic: Diffusion language-model decoding and low-step generation
why: The official abstract explicitly targets the hundreds-to-thousands of evaluations required by discrete diffusion language models and trains a discrete flow-matching model for configurable few-step generation. This is a direct text-generation latency/compute reduction.

title: FutureFill: Fast Generation from Convolutional Sequence Models
why: FutureFill reduces generation time from quadratic to quasilinear in context length and uses a prefill cache that scales with generated tokens rather than the prompt. The abstract validates substantial generation-efficiency gains, directly addressing decoding complexity and cache growth.

title: FZOO: Fast Zeroth-Order Optimizer for Fine‑Tuning Large Language Models towards Adam‑Scale Speed
topic: Memory- and step-efficient zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning
why: The official abstract reports three times fewer forward passes than MeZO on average and up to 18 times fewer for RoBERTa-large, with accuracy gains and Adam-scale convergence speed. It directly reduces fine-tuning compute and memory.

title: GAGA: Gaussianity-Aware Gaussian Approximation for Efficient 3D Molecular Generation
topic: Trajectory truncation for efficient 3D molecular generation
why: The official abstract replaces redundant portions of long stochastic generation trajectories with a closed-form Gaussian approximation while preserving full-resolution learning dynamics and improving computational efficiency.

title: GAPrune: Gradient-Alignment Pruning for Domain-Aware Embeddings
why: The official abstract reports one-shot 50% pruning with performance within 2.5% of dense models on FinMTEB/ChemTEB and gains after only 100 retraining steps. This is a direct, quantified embedding-compression result for resource-constrained deployment.

title: GAS: Improving Discretization of Diffusion ODEs via Generalized Adversarial Solver
why: The official abstract explicitly targets expensive diffusion sampling and distills ODE solvers from dozens of evaluations to only a few. Its generalized solver improves quality under similar resource constraints without extra training tricks, making it a direct inference-efficiency contribution.

title: Gelato: Graph Edit Distance via Autoregressive Neural Combinatorial Optimization
why: Gelato reports orders-of-magnitude faster graph-edit-distance solutions than competing ML-based methods while generalizing to larger graphs and reducing costly ground-truth needs. This is a direct algorithmic efficiency result

title: GenDR: Lighten Generative Detail Restoration
why: The official abstract explicitly targets lightening generative detail restoration, a direct generative-workload efficiency contribution. Retain as strong pending the primary-PDF review of its concrete compute and quality trade-offs.

title: Generalised Flow Maps for Few-Step Generative Modelling on Riemannian Manifolds
topic: Few-step flow-map generation on Riemannian manifolds
why: The first-party abstract explicitly targets the high inference cost of geometric generative models, introduces self-distilled few-step flow maps, and reports state-of-the-art single- and few-step sample quality across geometric datasets; this is a direct generation-acceleration contribution.

title: Glance and Focus Reinforcement for Pan-cancer Screening
why: GF-Screen reduces computation by 5.7× by selecting lesion-relevant regions and reports substantial validation gains. This is a direct, quantified inference-efficiency result with a clear practical deployment pathway.

title: GlowQ: Group-Shared LOw-Rank Approximation for Quantized LLMs
topic: Low-rank correction for quantized LLM serving
why: The official abstract reports GlowQ-S reducing TTFB by 23.4% and increasing throughput by 37.4% while maintaining accuracy within 0.2 percentage points.

title: Goedel-Prover-V2: Scaling Formal Theorem Proving with Scaffolded Data Synthesis and Self-Correction
topic: Compute-efficient LLM theorem proving and reasoning
why: The official abstract reports an 8B prover outperforming a 671B model and a 32B prover solving substantially more PutnamBench problems than a 671B baseline with about 20x smaller compute budget. This is a direct, quantified efficiency result for reasoning models.

title: GoldenStart: Q-Guided Priors and Entropy Control for Distilling Flow Policies
topic: One-step flow-policy distillation for efficient robot control
why: The official abstract explicitly targets prohibitive flow-policy inference latency and introduces Q-guided initialization for one-step generation. This directly accelerates distilled policies for continuous control and Physical AI.

title: GPG: A Simple and Strong Reinforcement Learning Baseline for Model Reasoning
why: The first-party abstract eliminates critic/reference models and KL constraints, simplifies GRPO-style training, and explicitly reports reduced computational costs with stronger performance across unimodal and multimodal tasks.

title: GPS: Graph-guided Proactive Information Seeking in Large Language Models
why: GPS models clarification logic as a DAG and dynamically prunes it using user responses, then trains the LLM with a reward balancing success and efficiency. The official abstract reports improved success rate and clarification efficiency on three benchmarks, directly relevant to efficient RAG/agent systems.

title: GPTailor: Large Language Model Pruning Through Layer Cutting and Stitching
why: GPTailor combines/removes layers from fine-tuned model variants to compress LLMs for deployment and inference. The official abstract reports about 25 percent fewer parameters while retaining approximately 97.3 percent of original performance, a direct model-compression result.

title: Gradient-Aligned Calibration for Post-Training Quantization of Diffusion Models
why: The official abstract directly identifies slow sampling and high memory use as deployment bottlenecks and proposes timestep-aware calibration for post-training quantization. This is a concrete diffusion inference efficiency method; retain as a strong individual record and attempt the official proceedings PDF.

title: Gradient-Sign Masking for Task Vector Transport Across Pre-Trained Models
why: The first-party abstract transfers task vectors across pretrained model releases using only a handful of labeled samples and a few gradients, with no parameter updates or additional fine-tuning. This directly avoids repeated training cost.

title: GradPruner: Gradient-guided Layer Pruning Enabling Efficient Fine-Tuning and Inference for LLMs
why: The official abstract targets fine-tuning cost and inference inefficiency of structured pruning and introduces early-gradient layer importance to prune during downstream fine-tuning. This directly reduces training and inference cost.

title: Graph Diffusion Transformers are In-Context Molecular Designers
topic: Compact graph-tokenization and in-context molecular diffusion
why: The official abstract introduces motif-level Node Pair Encoding that requires 5.5x fewer nodes and a 0.7B molecular model matching or exceeding models 100–1000x larger across 33 design tasks. These are direct representation/model-size efficiency signals.

title: Graph Signal Processing Meets Mamba2: Adaptive Filter Bank via Delta Modulation
why: HADES structures Mamba2 as a hierarchical adaptive filter bank and reports comparable benchmark performance using only 58.9 percent of the original parameters. This is a direct efficient sequence-model architecture contribution for language and long-context workloads.

title: GraphPlanner: Graph Memory-Augmented Agentic Routing for Multi-Agent LLMs
topic: Cost-efficient routing for multi-agent LLM inference
why: The official abstract reports up to 9.3 percent higher accuracy while reducing GPU cost from 186.26 GiB to 1.04 GiB through learned workflow and model routing. This is a direct, quantified efficient-agent systems contribution.

title: Group Critical-token Policy Optimization for Autoregressive Image Generation
topic: critical-token optimization for AR image generation
why: The official abstract reports that optimizing only 30% of image tokens outperforms full-token GRPO on text-to-image benchmarks. This is direct training-token and compute efficiency for image generation.

title: Group-Normalized Implicit Value Optimization for Language Models
why: GN-IVO removes the auxiliary critic network and its computational overhead by learning step-level values implicitly through group-normalized distribution matching. The official abstract provides a direct training-efficiency mechanism while preserving the optimal policy.

title: Guided Query Refinement: Multimodal Hybrid Retrieval with Test-Time Optimization
why: The official abstract reports matching larger-representation model performance while achieving up to 14× faster retrieval and 54× lower memory. This is a direct, quantified multimodal efficiency contribution.

title: Guided Speculative Inference for Efficient Test-Time Alignment of LLMs
topic: reward-guided speculative inference for LLM reasoning
why: The official abstract combines soft best-of-n test-time scaling with speculative samples and reports up to 28% lower end-to-end latency while improving reward-guided accuracy. This directly targets efficient reasoning inference.

title: GuirlVG: Incentivize GUI Visual Grounding via Empirical Exploration on Reinforcement Learning
why: The official abstract reports 5.2K RL training samples outperforming SFT methods trained on over 10M samples, with +7.7%/+17.2% gains on ScreenSpot/Pro. This is direct post-training data efficiency.

title: Half-order Fine-Tuning for Diffusion Model: A Recursive Likelihood Ratio Optimizer
why: The official abstract introduces a specialized recursive likelihood-ratio optimizer for diffusion-model fine-tuning. This is a direct training-optimization contribution in the diffusion/flow acceleration landscape.

title: Hallucination Reduction with CASAL:  Contrastive Activation Steering for Amortized Learning
why: CASAL bakes activation steering into model weights, avoiding real-time inference monitoring/intervention. The abstract reports roughly 30–40 percent hallucination reduction and about 30 times compute efficiency and 20 times data efficiency versus LoRA baselines, directly supporting practical deployment.

title: HEAPr: Hessian-based Efficient Atomic Expert Pruning in Output Space
why: The official abstract reduces pruning-importance computation from O(d^4) to O(d^2) and reports nearly lossless compression across DeepSeek and Qwen MoE models.

title: Heterogeneous Federated Fine-Tuning with Parallel One-Rank Adaptation
why: The official abstract introduces lightweight parallel one-rank adapters and a folding strategy for clients with different resources, reporting improved accuracy and efficiency. This directly targets distributed fine-tuning under heterogeneous memory and compute.

title: HiDrop: Hierarchical Vision Token Reduction in MLLMs via Late Injection, Concave Pyramid Pruning, and Early Exit
topic: Vision-token pruning and efficient MLLM inference
why: HiDrop combines late token injection, dynamic pyramid pruning, and early exit, with FlashAttention-compatible selection to avoid hidden overhead. The official abstract reports about 90 percent visual-token compression at matched performance and 1.72 times faster training, directly targeting efficient MLLM execution.

title: Hierarchy Decoding: A Training-free Parallel Decoding Strategy  for Diffusion Large Language Models
topic: Parallel decoding for diffusion LLM inference
why: The official abstract reports up to 17x faster decoding than vanilla dLLM and about 1.5x faster than Fast-dLLM at comparable or better accuracy.

title: HiGS: History-Guided Sampling for Plug-and-Play Enhancement of Diffusion Models
why: The official abstract says HiGS reuses recent predictions with practically no additional computation and reaches ImageNet FID 1.61 with 30 sampling steps instead of 250. This is a direct, quantified diffusion-inference efficiency method.

title: Hilbert-Guided Sparse Local Attention
topic: block-sparse local attention for high-resolution vision
why: The official abstract identifies quadratic attention compute/memory and poor block-sparse locality, then reorders tokens along a Hilbert curve to improve block sparsity and kernel efficiency. This is a direct attention/kernel optimization.

title: HippoTune: A Hippocampal Associative Loop–Inspired Fine-Tuning Method for Continual Learning
why: The first-party abstract reports a 50% reduction in training FLOPs while improving accuracy by 5–8 points over buffer-free PEFT-CL methods. This is a direct, quantified training-efficiency contribution under tight compute constraints.

title: HiPRAG: Hierarchical Process Rewards for Efficient Agentic Retrieval Augmented Generation
topic: Efficient agentic RAG and search control
why: The official abstract directly targets unnecessary retrieval overhead and reports reducing over-search from above 27% to 2.3% while lowering under-search and improving accuracy. This is a strong measured reasoning-agent efficiency result.

title: Hybrid Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
topic: Training VLAs to skip chain-of-thought at inference while retaining its benefits
why: The first-party abstract explicitly notes CoT increases inference time and proposes hybrid training that lets VLAs benefit from thoughts while omitting CoT generation during action inference; this is a direct, high-value latency reduction for protected Physical AI.

title: Hyden: A Hybrid Dual-Path Encoder for Monocular Geometry of High-resolution Images
why: The official abstract combines a fixed-resolution ViT with a full-resolution CNN and reports state-of-the-art high-resolution geometry with the lowest inference latency among competitors. It directly reduces high-resolution vision inference cost.

title: Hyper-SET: Designing Transformers via Hyperspherical Energy Minimization
topic: Compact recurrent-depth Transformer with shared parameters
why: The official abstract introduces a recurrent-depth Transformer with shared parameters across layers, scaling depth with fewer parameters while maintaining competitive performance and offering linear-attention variants; this is a substantive model-efficiency contribution.

title: Hyperspherical Latents Improve Continuous-Token Autoregressive Generation
topic: Parameter-efficient autoregressive image generation with hyperspherical latents
why: The first-party abstract reports a 208M-parameter model matching a 2B-parameter baseline and a 943M model achieving FID 1.34, directly improving the quality/parameter tradeoff for autoregressive image generation.

title: ICaRus: Identical Cache Reuse for Efficient Multi-Model Inference
topic: multi-model LLM serving / cross-model KV cache reuse
why: ICLR 2026 Poster. Shares identical KV caches across specialized models; official ICLR proceedings reports up to 11.1x lower P95 latency and 3.8x higher throughput in 8-model multi-agent scenarios.

title: IceCache: Memory-Efficient KV-cache Management for Long-Sequence LLMs
topic: KV cache / CPU-GPU offload / long-context inference
why: ICLR 2026 direct long-context KV-management work integrating semantic clustering with PagedAttention for CPU-GPU offload; maintains 99% full-cache accuracy with a 256-token budget and competitive latency.

title: iLLaVA: An Image is Worth Fewer Than 1/3 Input Tokens in Large Multimodal Models
topic: Visual-token reduction for efficient MLLM inference
why: The official abstract explicitly targets fewer than one-third of the input tokens for an image in large multimodal models. This is a direct token-reduction approach to lower downstream MLLM inference cost.

title: Improved Adversarial Diffusion Compression for Real-World Video Super-Resolution
topic: diffusion-model compression and video inference acceleration
why: The official abstract identifies multi-step and heavy diffusion inference as the bottleneck, then reports 95% parameter-complexity reduction and 8x acceleration over the DOVE teacher while preserving competitive video quality. This is a direct deployment-efficiency result.

title: Improving and Accelerating Offline RL in Large Discrete Action Spaces with Structured Policy Initialization
topic: accelerating offline RL in combinatorial action spaces
why: The official abstract identifies slow and unstable joint-action learning, then pretrains a valid-action structure model and trains lightweight policy heads. It reports up to 12.8x faster convergence and up to 39% higher return, a direct and quantified RL-training efficiency contribution; promote strongly.

title: Improving Block-Wise LLM Quantization by 4-bit Block-Wise Optimal Float (BOF4): Analysis and Variations
why: The official abstract targets memory-efficient fine-tuning and inference and introduces optimized 4-bit quantizers with outlier-preserving mixed precision to reduce quantization error.

title: In-Context Multi-Objective Optimization
topic: amortized transformer optimization for expensive black-box objectives
why: The official abstract replaces per-task surrogate fitting and acquisition engineering with a pretrained in-context optimizer, proposing each design in one forward pass. It reports 50–1000x lower proposal time while matching or improving Pareto quality, a direct quantified optimization-efficiency contribution; promote strongly.

title: Inconsistency Biases in Dynamic Data Pruning
why: RePB corrects score-context drift and temporal gradient bias in dynamic data pruning. The official abstract reports near-full-dataset accuracy using substantially reduced data across 16 datasets, 17 models, and 13 tasks, directly targeting efficient deep-learning training.

title: IncVGGT: Incremental VGGT for Memory-Bounded Long-Range 3D Reconstruction
why: IncVGGT fuses overlapping frames and prunes history to bound cache growth. The official abstract reports 58.5 times fewer operators, 9 times lower memory, 25.7 times less energy, and 4.9 times faster inference on 500-frame sequences, while supporting 10k-frame inputs; this is a direct efficient 3D/world-model systems contribution.

title: Inference-Cost-Aware Dynamic Tree Construction for Efficient Inference in Large Language Models
why: ICLR 2026 Poster; CAST incorporates GPU and batch-dependent inference cost into dynamic speculative trees and reports up to 5.2x speedup.

title: InfLLM-V2: Dense-Sparse Switchable Attention for Seamless Short-to-Long Adaptation
topic: trainable sparse attention for long-context LLMs
why: The official abstract targets long-sequence compute/memory bottlenecks and introduces dense-sparse switchable attention while preserving the short-context pretrain/long-context finetune workflow. This directly addresses long-context inference and training efficiency.

title: Influence-Preserving Proxies for Gradient-Based Data Selection in LLM FineTuning
topic: Compute-reduced gradient-based data selection for LLM fine-tuning
why: The official abstract constructs influence-preserving compressed proxies and reports more than half the computational cost reduction relative to the full 3B model while outperforming baselines. This directly makes gradient-based data selection scalable.

title: InfoScan: Information-Efficient Visual Scanning via Resource-Adaptive Walks
why: The first-party abstract allocates compute dynamically to salient image regions and reports superior efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs over fixed scanning. This directly targets high-resolution vision compute.

title: InftyThink: Breaking the Length Limits of Long-Context Reasoning in Large Language Models
why: The official abstract interleaves reasoning segments with summaries to bound computational and memory growth and reports lower computational cost with 3 to 11 percent benchmark improvements. This directly improves long-context reasoning efficiency.

title: Investigating Redundancy in Multimodal Large Language Models with Multiple Vision Encoders
topic: Efficient MLLM architecture and encoder pruning
why: The official abstract demonstrates pervasive encoder redundancy, with single/dual-encoder variants recovering over 90% of baseline on most tasks and up to 3.6% overall accuracy improvement over the full model. This directly supports efficient multimodal architecture reduction.

title: Is Finer Better? The Limits of Microscaling Formats in Large Language Models
why: The paper analyzes FP4 microscaling failure modes and proposes UE5M3 scales, retaining comparable performance to E4M3 while eliminating global scaling operations on weights and activations. This is a direct hardware-aware quantization and execution-efficiency contribution.

title: IVC-Prune: Revealing the Implicit Visual Coordinates in LVLMs for Vision Token Pruning
why: IVC-Prune is a training-free prompt-aware pruning method that preserves implicit spatial-coordinate tokens and relevant foreground tokens. The official abstract reports about 50 percent fewer visual tokens while retaining at least 99 percent of original performance across four LVLMs and twenty benchmarks, directly reducing high-resolution inference cost.

title: Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma Guided Network for Efficient 3D Medical Segmentation
why: The official abstract reports 11x GPU and 48x CPU throughput, 1/20 peak training GPU memory, and 1/24 inference cost with improved Dice performance.

title: KaLM-Embedding-V2: Superior Training Techniques and Data Inspire A Versatile Embedding Model
topic: Compact sub-billion embedding models with large-model-level capability
why: The official abstract reports compact 0.5B embedding models that rival models 3–26 times larger through training/data improvements, directly improving the quality/parameter tradeoff for embedding inference.

title: KBVQ-MoE: KLT-guided SVD with Bias-Corrected Vector Quantization for MoE Large Language Models
topic: low-bit vector quantization for MoE LLM deployment
why: The official abstract identifies MoE parameter/memory demands and introduces expert-aware vector quantization to improve codebook utilization and reduce compression error. This directly targets model compression and deployment efficiency.

title: KDP: Simplifying Representation Dynamics in Kernel Space
why: KDP identifies computational redundancy in consecutive LLM layers and learns a kernel-space inverse transformation to prune entire layer blocks. The official abstract validates it against pruning baselines, making it a direct LLM deployment-compression method.

title: Knowing When to Quit: Probabilistic Early Exits for Speech Separation Networks
topic: Adaptive-compute speech inference and early exit
why: The first-party abstract introduces calibrated probabilistic early exits and explicitly reports considerable test-time compute savings through dynamic compute scaling without compromising reconstruction. This is a direct adaptive-inference efficiency contribution.

title: Knowledge Exchange with Confidence: Cost-Effective LLM Integration for Reliable and Efficient Visual Question Answering
topic: Confidence-based model routing for efficient VQA inference
why: The official abstract routes specialized questions to a task-specific model and general questions to an LLM using confidence, explicitly improving inference speed and reducing computational cost while increasing reliability. This is a direct efficient multimodal serving method.

title: KV-Cache Transform Coding for Compact Storage in LLM Inference
topic: KV cache compression / LLM serving storage
why: PCA, adaptive quantization and entropy coding for reusable KV-cache storage; official ICLR paper reports up to 20x compression while maintaining reasoning/long-context accuracy, with higher ratios in selected use cases.

title: KVComm: Enabling Efficient LLM Communication through Selective KV Sharing
topic: Selective KV-cache sharing for multi-agent LLM communication
why: The official abstract reports preserving near-upper-bound task performance while transmitting as few as 30% of KV layers' pairs, reducing inter-model communication payload and inference cost.

title: Language-Instructed Vision Embeddings for Controllable and Generalizable Perception
topic: Task-adaptive vision embeddings without task-specific retraining
why: The official abstract reports instruction-guided visual embeddings that outperform VLMs with orders of magnitude more parameters on VQA and generalize without task-specific retraining, directly improving model-size and adaptation efficiency for perception.

title: LapFlow: Laplacian Multi-scale Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
why: The official abstract reports parallel multiscale generation without inter-scale renoising, with fewer GFLOPs and faster inference than baselines. This is a direct and explicit generative-inference efficiency contribution.

title: LaplacianFormer:Rethinking Linear Attention with Laplacian Kernel
topic: linear attention and custom CUDA kernels
why: The official abstract targets quadratic softmax attention and costly low-rank operations, using a Laplacian kernel, Nyström approximation, Newton–Schulz iteration, and custom CUDA kernels. This is a direct efficient-attention/kernel contribution.

title: Large Language Model Compression with Global Rank and Sparsity Optimization
topic: Joint low-rank and sparse LLM compression
why: The method jointly allocates rank and sparsity across layers to compress LLM weights and reduce optimization search. The official abstract directly targets model compression and surpasses state-of-the-art sparsification/composite-approximation baselines, making it a strong deployment-efficiency record.

title: LaSeR: Reinforcement Learning with Last-Token Self-Rewarding
topic: Low-overhead self-verification for efficient LLM reasoning
why: The official abstract replaces a separate self-verification generation with a last-token score and adds at most one token inference after solution generation. This directly removes the roughly doubled inference cost of prior self-rewarding approaches.

title: Late-to-Early Training: LET LLMs Learn Earlier, So Faster and Better
why: The official abstract reports up to 1.6x training speedup and nearly 5% downstream accuracy improvement for a 1.4B model, using a pretrained model with 10x fewer parameters. This is a direct, quantified LLM training-efficiency contribution.

title: Latent Adaptation of Foundation Policies for Sim-to-Real Transfer
why: The official abstract explicitly avoids resource-intensive policy retraining and costly policy optimization by adapting latent representations with a small adapter and target-domain data. This is a strong deployment/training-efficiency contribution with protected Physical-AI relevance.

title: Latent Speech-Text Transformer
topic: Latent speech-token aggregation for efficient speech-text modeling
why: The official abstract aggregates long speech-token sequences into latent patches and reports reduced computational cost and shorter autoregressive sequences for ASR/TTS inference without reconstruction-quality loss. This is a direct multimodal sequence-efficiency method.

title: Latent-Guided Reasoning: Empowering Small LLMs with Large-Model Thinking
why: The first-party abstract separates large-model planning from small-model execution using compact latent guidance and improves the performance-cost tradeoff for 0.5B–8B models. This directly targets reasoning cost.

title: LD-EnSF: Synergizing Latent Dynamics with Ensemble Score Filters for Fast Data Assimilation with Sparse Observations
topic: Latent-space acceleration for score-based data assimilation
why: The official abstract eliminates full-space simulations by evolving dynamics in a compact latent space and reports speedups of orders of magnitude while maintaining accuracy. This is a direct, high-impact scientific-ML acceleration result.

title: Learn to Reason Efficiently with Adaptive Length-based Reward Shaping
why: The official abstract reports LASER-D improving AIME2024 by 5.3 points while reducing token usage by 64% across reasoning models. This is direct inference-cost reduction with quality retained.

title: Learnable Sparsity for Vision Generative Models
topic: End-to-end pruning of diffusion and flow generative models
why: The official abstract reports pruning 20% of SDXL and FLUX parameters in 10 A100 GPU-hours and introduces checkpointing to make end-to-end pruning fit a limited memory budget.

title: Learning an Image Editing Model without Image Editing Pairs
topic: Few-step diffusion image editing without paired training data
why: The first-party abstract directly optimizes a few-step diffusion editor and reports parity with paired-data-trained models while eliminating paired data, with performance over Flow-GRPO; this is a high-value generation/training-efficiency contribution.

title: Learning More with Less: A Dynamic Dual-Level Down-Sampling Framework for Efficient Policy Optimization
topic: Sample- and token-efficient RL policy optimization
why: The official abstract introduces theoretically motivated rollout- and token-level down-sampling with a dynamic schedule, and reports state-of-the-art generalization using fewer samples and tokens on Qwen2.5 and Llama3.1. This is a direct efficient policy-optimization contribution.

title: Learning Posterior Predictive Distributions for Node Classification from Synthetic Graph Priors
topic: Universal graph node classification without graph-specific training
why: The first-party abstract trains NodePFN on synthetic graph priors and generalizes to arbitrary graphs without graph-specific training, directly reducing per-graph adaptation/training requirements across 23 benchmarks; this is a substantive training-efficiency contribution.

title: Learning Retrieval Models with Sparse Autoencoders
topic: Sparse latent retrieval and compact multilingual retrieval models
why: SPLARE uses sparse-autoencoder latent features as query/document indexing units for learned sparse retrieval and releases a 2B-parameter variant with a lighter footprint. The official abstract reports strong multilingual/out-of-domain retrieval, directly relevant to efficient retrieval systems.

title: Learning To Draft: Adaptive Speculative Decoding with Reinforcement Learning
why: The official abstract identifies static draft/verify time allocation as a bottleneck and trains co-adaptive policies to optimize throughput per draft-and-verify cycle. This is a direct LLM inference acceleration method.

title: Learning to Parallel: Accelerating Diffusion Large Language Models via Learnable Parallel Decoding
topic: learnable parallel decoding for diffusion LLM inference
why: The official abstract identifies sequential decoding throughput limits and proposes a learned filter to adaptively unmask tokens in parallel, directly improving dLLM inference speed-quality trade-offs.

title: Learning to Reason over Continuous Tokens with Reinforcement Learning
topic: Hybrid latent reasoning for token-efficient LLM inference
why: The official abstract dynamically switches between explicit and latent reasoning and reports significant token-usage reductions while maintaining or improving accuracy. This directly targets the compute and memory cost of verbose chain-of-thought.

title: Learning to Segment for Vehicle Routing Problems
topic: learning-guided acceleration of iterative vehicle-routing solvers
why: The official abstract identifies redundant recomputation of stable VRP solution segments and introduces learned segmentation to aggregate them while searching only unstable portions. It reports 2x–7x solver acceleration across CVRP and VRPTW and supports traditional, learned, and hybrid solvers; promote strongly.

title: LeSTD: LLM Compression via Learning-based Sparse Tensor Decomposition
topic: Sparse tensor decomposition for LLM compression
why: LeSTD jointly represents attention heads with a shared basis and learns an ultra-sparse core tensor, addressing the dense-core storage bottleneck in post-training tensor decomposition. The official abstract directly targets higher-ratio LLM weight compression for deployment.

title: Libra: Effective yet Efficient Load Balancing for Large-scale MoE Inference
why: The official abstract describes prediction-based expert load balancing with overlapped overhead and reports up to 19.2% throughput improvement on large-scale MoE inference. This is a direct serving-system contribution.

title: LiFR-Seg: Anytime High-Frame-Rate Segmentation via Event-Guided Propagation
topic: Resource-efficient high-frame-rate perception with event-guided propagation
why: The official abstract achieves 73.82% mIoU on DSEC, within 0.09% of a high-frame-rate upper bound, while using low-frame-rate RGB plus asynchronous events. This is a direct efficient-perception result for resource-constrained/Physical-AI settings.

title: LightRetriever: A LLM-based Text Retrieval Architecture with Extremely Faster Query Inference
topic: Lightweight online query encoding for LLM retrieval
why: The official abstract reports over 1000x query-encoding speedup and over 10x end-to-end retrieval throughput while retaining an average of 95% retrieval performance.

title: LinearSR: Unlocking Linear Attention for Stable and Efficient Image Super-Resolution
topic: linear attention for efficient image super-resolution
why: The official abstract targets quadratic self-attention cost in generative image super-resolution and introduces a framework using linear attention with stability and quality controls. This is directly relevant to image-generation acceleration.

title: LLaVA-FA: Learning Fourier Approximation for Compressing Large Multimodal Models
topic: Joint low-rank and quantization compression for LMMs
why: The official abstract jointly applies frequency-domain low-rank approximation and quantization to reduce multimodal-model weights, with compact representations, minimal activated parameters, and low compute. This is a direct efficient-MLLM compression contribution.

title: Local Linear Attention: An Optimal Interpolation of Linear and Softmax Attention For Test-Time Regression
topic: Hardware-efficient linear attention and customized inference kernels
why: The official abstract introduces memory-efficient primitives, a hardware-efficient blockwise FlashLLA algorithm, and a customized inference kernel to reduce memory overhead and enable scalable parallel computation.

title: LogART: Pushing the Limit of Efficient Logarithmic Post-Training Quantization
why: The official abstract targets deployment efficiency and introduces learnable logarithmic rounding with outlier-aware, asymmetric, hardware-friendly dynamic bases. This directly advances model compression and quantized inference.

title: Logit‑KL Flow Matching: Non‑Autoregressive Text Generation via Sampling‑Hybrid Inference
topic: non-autoregressive text generation and hybrid sampling
why: The official abstract motivates NAR text generation as a way to avoid sequential autoregressive decoding and proposes KL-geodesic flow matching with hybrid inference. This directly targets generation efficiency.

title: Long-Context Attention Benchmark: From Kernel Efficiency to Distributed Context Parallelism
topic: efficient attention / distributed context parallelism / benchmark
why: ICLR 2026 unified benchmark spanning attention kernels and distributed context parallelism, evaluated up to 96 GPUs; directly relevant to kernel/distributed efficiency selection.

title: Long-Context Generalization with Sparse Attention
topic: adaptive sparse attention for long-context transformers
why: The official abstract introduces learnable entmax-based sparse attention to suppress irrelevant tokens and improve long-context pattern focus. This directly targets attention compute and long-context efficiency.

title: LookaheadKV: Fast and Accurate KV Cache Eviction by Glimpsing into the Future without Generation
topic: low-overhead KV-cache eviction for long-context inference
why: The official abstract identifies expensive draft generation in future-aware KV eviction and proposes a cheaper predictive signal to improve cache retention without generating a surrogate response. This directly targets KV-cache memory and prefill overhead.

title: Lookup multivariate Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
topic: Lookup-based efficient neural layers and CUDA kernels
why: lmKAN replaces costly high-dimensional linear mappings with low-dimensional spline lookup functions. The official abstract reports up to 6 times fewer inference FLOPs, over 10 times H100 throughput at equal accuracy on one benchmark, and 1.6–2.1 times lower CNN FLOPs with matched accuracy; this is a direct architecture/kernel efficiency result.

title: LouisKV: Efficient KV Cache Retrieval for Long Input-Output Sequences
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / retrieval / Triton-CUDA kernels
why: ICLR 2026 poster. LouisKV exploits temporal locality and semantic boundaries for fine-grained KV retrieval across long input/output sequences, with custom Triton/CUDA kernels; the ICLR paper reports up to 4.7x speedup over prior KV retrieval while retaining near-lossless accuracy.

title: Low-Latency Neural LiDAR Compression with 2D Context Models
why: The official abstract replaces computationally intensive 3D contexts with 2D context models and reports significant gains in both rate-distortion performance and coding speed. It directly targets compression latency and redundant computation in an edge/perception workload.

title: LSA: Layer-wise Sparsity Allocation for Large Language Model Pruning Based on Minimal Linear Reconstruction Error
why: LSA allocates non-uniform sparsity by layer/block/projection using minimal reconstruction error. The official abstract reports strong performance at 70 percent overall sparsity across language modeling and seven zero-shot tasks, a direct LLM compression and deployment-efficiency result.

title: MAGO: Beyond Fixed Hyperparameters with Multi-Objective Pareto Optimization for Hybrid LLM Reasoning
topic: Adaptive hybrid reasoning and LLM token efficiency
why: The first-party abstract reports 2.2x–3x token-efficiency gains with 0.6%–9.4% relative accuracy improvements by adapting reasoning mode to query complexity. This is a direct, quantified efficient-reasoning contribution.

title: Making Slow Thinking Faster: Compressing LLM Chain-of-Thought via Step Entropy
why: The method learns to skip low-entropy redundant reasoning steps and reports that 80 percent of such steps can be pruned without significant accuracy loss. Its SFT/GRPO training enables compressed CoT generation at inference, directly reducing reasoning tokens and inference cost.

title: Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles
topic: efficient sequence model architecture / state-space model / constant-memory decode / inference-first linear model
why: ICLR 2026 inference-first state-space architecture by Albert Gu, Tri Dao, J. Zico Kolter and collaborators. Mamba-3 targets the quality/efficiency frontier of linear-time constant-memory sequence models and introduces expressive recurrence, complex-valued state updates and MIMO structure without increasing decode latency; this is mandatory canonical lineage for efficient inference architecture.

title: MambaVoiceCloning: Efficient and Expressive Text-to-Speech via State-Space Modeling and Diffusion Control
why: The official abstract describes linear-time SSM-only conditioning with bounded activation memory and reports 1.6x throughput improvement, while explicitly noting diffusion remains the dominant latency source.

title: Mango-GS: Enhancing Spatio-Temporal Consistency in Dynamic Scenes Reconstruction using Multi-Frame Node-Guided 4D Gaussian Splatting
why: Mango-GS confines temporal modeling to sparse control nodes and reports fast rendering with real-time dynamic-scene reconstruction. This is a direct efficiency contribution for 4D scene/world modeling and Physical-AI-adjacent workloads.

title: MarS-FM: Generative Modeling of Molecular Dynamics via Markov State Models
topic: Flow-matching surrogate generation for computationally expensive molecular dynamics
why: The official abstract reports more than two orders of magnitude speedup over implicit- or explicit-solvent molecular-dynamics simulations while reproducing structural observables. This is a directly quantified generative-computation acceleration result with clear high-value reading relevance.

title: Masked Generative Policy for Robotic Control
topic: parallel masked action generation for robot policies
