why: The official abstract proposes parallel action-token generation, refinement only of low-confidence tokens, and single-pass full-trajectory prediction. This directly concerns efficient action inference and is protected Physical AI.

title: MaskPro: Linear-Space Probabilistic Learning for Strict (N:M)-Sparsity on LLMs
why: The official abstract targets inference efficiency through strict N:M sparsity and presents a linear-space probabilistic method designed to improve memory scalability and hardware-friendly acceleration.

title: MASS: MoErging through Adaptive Subspace Selection
why: MASS combines task-specific low-rank subspaces without retraining, recovers up to about 98% of endpoint accuracy, and uses a fixed roughly 2x storage factor instead of storing every model. This is a direct quantified model-storage efficiency result

title: Massive Memorization with Hundreds of Trillions of Parameters for Sequential Transducer Generative Recommenders
why: VISTA summarizes up to million-item user histories into a few hundred cached tokens, keeping downstream training and inference costs fixed while improving offline/online metrics. The official abstract reports industrial deployment at billion-user scale, directly targeting latency, QPS, and GPU-cost scalability.

title: Mastering Sparse CUDA Generation through Pretrained Models and Deep Reinforcement Learning
why: SparseRL generates CUDA code for sparse matrix operations using execution-efficiency rewards. The official abstract reports a 20 percent higher compilation rate and 30 percent faster SpMV code on average, directly targeting GPU kernel performance.

title: Matched Data, Better Models: Target Aligned Data Filtering with Sparse Autoencoders
why: SDM selects target-aligned image-caption subsets using sparse-autoencoder features and submodular optimization. The official abstract reports performance within 1 percent of state of the art while using over 5 times fewer GPU hours than the leading approach, a direct training-efficiency result.

title: MatRIS: Toward Reliable and Efficient Pretrained Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
topic: Linear-complexity attention for efficient interatomic potentials
why: The official abstract introduces separable O(N) attention for three-body interactions and reports comparable benchmark accuracy at lower training cost than leading equivariant MLIPs. This is a direct scientific-ML efficiency result.

title: Mean Flow Policy with Instantaneous Velocity Constraint for One-step Action Generation
topic: one-step flow policy inference for robot manipulation
why: The official abstract explicitly targets computational burden from multiple flow steps and introduces one-step action generation with reported training and inference speed improvements on robotic manipulation tasks.

title: MeanCache: From Instantaneous to Average Velocity for Accelerating Flow Matching Inference
why: The official abstract introduces a training-free cache for flow-matching inference, stable trajectory scheduling, and JVP reuse, with measured multi-fold acceleration on FLUX, Qwen-Image, and HunyuanVideo. This is a direct diffusion/flow acceleration contribution.

title: MEGS^{2}: Memory-Efficient Gaussian Splatting via Spherical Gaussians and Unified Pruning
topic: 3D Gaussian Splatting memory reduction and edge deployment
why: The official abstract reports 50% static-VRAM and 40% rendering-VRAM reductions while maintaining comparable quality, directly addressing the rendering-memory bottleneck.

title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
topic: constant-context memory consolidation for long-horizon agents
why: The official abstract maintains near-constant context size and reports 3.7x lower memory usage with 3.5x performance versus a larger instruction model. This directly improves long-horizon agent efficiency.

title: Merge before Forget: A Single LoRA Continual Learning via Continual Merging
why: Merge-before-Forget merges continual task updates into one LoRA and maintains constant memory complexity as task count grows. This is a direct LLM adaptation-memory efficiency contribution

title: Meta-UCF: Unified Task-Conditioned LoRA Generation for Continual Learning in Large Language Models
why: The official abstract generates task-specific LoRA updates from a single hypernetwork and uses one adapter across an unbounded task stream, avoiding linear parameter growth and inner-loop gradients. This directly targets low-resource continual adaptation.

title: Metis: Training LLMs with FP4 Quantization
topic: FP4 quantization for large-scale LLM training
why: The official abstract reports W4A4G4 training of LLaMA-3 8B with only 0.4% training-loss gap and 0.1% downstream-accuracy degradation versus BF16, with lower overhead than Nvidia's FP4 recipe.

title: MicroMix: Efficient Mixed-Precision Quantization with Microscaling Formats for Large Language Models
topic: MXFP mixed-precision quantization and GEMM kernels
why: The official abstract co-designs MXFP4/6/8 quantization with Blackwell Tensor-Core GEMM kernels to exploit low-precision hardware throughput for LLM inference. This is a direct model-compression and kernel-acceleration contribution.

title: MILPnet: A Multi-Scale Architecture with Geometric Feature Sequence Representations for Advancing MILP Problems
topic: Parameter-efficient neural architecture for faster MILP solving
why: The first-party abstract reports fewer parameters and faster convergence than graph-based baselines, with end-to-end solver integration on real MILP benchmarks; this is a direct optimization-efficiency contribution.

title: MIRA: Memory-Integrated Reinforcement Learning Agent  with Limited LLM Guidance
topic: Amortized LLM guidance for efficient RL agents
why: MIRA stores LLM-derived guidance in a persistent memory graph and amortizes queries instead of requiring continuous online LLM supervision. The official abstract reports comparable returns to frequent-LLM-guidance methods while requiring substantially fewer online LLM queries, a direct agent-system cost reduction.

title: MIRACLE: Model-free Imitation and Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cut-Selection
why: MIRACLE reports 3.78x average speedup on MIPLIB and 98.1% lower memory, reducing peak use from 3.03 GB to 46 MB while retaining a competitive objective gap. This is a direct quantified efficiency result

title: Mitigating Privacy Risk via Forget Set-Free Unlearning
why: Reload performs partially blind unlearning without retaining the forget set, using gradient optimization and structured weight sparsification. The official abstract reports Llama2-7B unlearning in under 8 minutes with under 0.025 percent of the retain set and under 7 percent of model weights, a direct efficient ML-operations result.

title: MixLinear: Extreme Low Resource Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with $0.1K$ Parameters
topic: Low-resource time-series forecasting with structural sparsity and low-rank spectral filtering
why: The official abstract targets compute-constrained forecasting, reduces the parameter scale from O(n^2) to O(n), and uses an ultra-low-dimensional frequency latent space. This is a direct efficient-model contribution with clear resource-constrained deployment relevance.

title: Mixture of Contexts for Long Video Generation
topic: Sparse attention routing and long-context video-generation efficiency
why: The official abstract identifies quadratic self-attention as the long-video compute/memory bottleneck and introduces sparse context routing with near-linear scaling. This is a direct algorithmic complexity and inference/training efficiency contribution.

title: Mixture-of-Experts Can Surpass Dense LLMs Under Strictly Equal Resource
topic: Resource-efficient MoE architecture and LLM training
why: The first-party abstract demonstrates that an MoE can outperform a dense counterpart under equal total parameters, training compute, and data budget, with extensive 2B/7B-scale experiments. This is a core efficient-architecture result.

title: MLP Memory: A Retriever-Pretrained Memory for Large Language Models
topic: Parametric retrieval memory for low-latency LLM inference
why: The official abstract internalizes retrieval patterns in a lightweight MLP module and reports 2.5 times faster inference than RAG with better accuracy. This is a direct alternative to latency-heavy retrieval-based knowledge access.

title: MMTok: Multimodal Coverage Maximization for Efficient Inference of VLMs
topic: Multimodal visual-token pruning for VLM inference
why: The official abstract reports a 1.87x speedup on LLaVA-NeXT-13B while preserving 98.7% of original POPE performance through multimodal coverage-based token selection.

title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for Non-Interactive Secure Transformer Inference
why: The official abstract removes 2448 HE rotations, uses at least 1.7 times fewer rotations, and reduces secure-transformer evaluation time by 52.8 percent versus THOR. This is a direct, quantified secure-inference systems contribution.

title: MoBE: Mixture-of-Basis-Experts for Compressing MoE-based LLMs
why: MoBE shares basis matrices across experts to compress very large MoE models. The official abstract reports 24–30 percent parameter reduction on Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3-671B, and Kimi-K2-1T with only about 1–2 percent relative accuracy drop, directly addressing deployment memory.

title: MobiEdit: Resource-efficient Knowledge Editing for Personalized On-device LLMs
why: The official abstract reports real-time editing of 3B models on commercial mobile devices with 7.1x less memory, 15.8x less energy, and 3.4x less latency than prior editing methods.

title: Mobile-GS: Real-time Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Devices
why: Mobile-GS removes depth sorting from alpha blending and combines vector quantization with contribution-based pruning to compact the Gaussian representation. The official abstract reports real-time rendering and compact model size on mobile/edge devices, directly targeting efficient 3D inference.

title: MobileKGQA: On-Device KGQA System on Dynamic Mobile Environments
why: MobileKGQA uses 7.2% of the computation and 9% of parameters versus SOTA, while achieving 20.3% higher performance at 30.4% of energy on Jetson Orin Nano. This is a direct edge-efficiency result

title: MobileLLM-R1: Exploring the Limits of Sub-Billion Language Model Reasoners with Open Training Recipes
topic: Data- and parameter-efficient sub-billion reasoning models
why: The official abstract reports strong reasoning from a 950M model using 11.7% of the pretraining tokens of a 36T-token reference corpus, with about 2T high-quality tokens sufficient for data curation. This is a direct data/model-scale efficiency contribution.

title: MoL: Adaptive Mixture-of-Length Reasoning for Efficient Question Answering with Context
topic: difficulty-adaptive response length and inference-cost reduction
why: The first-party abstract explicitly targets response efficiency and reports competitive QA accuracy with substantially fewer tokens through difficulty-aware length modulation. This directly reduces inference cost.

title: MoM: Linear Sequence Modeling with Mixture-of-Memories
why: MoM adds routed independent memory states to linear sequence models while retaining linear training complexity and constant-complexity inference. The official abstract reports improved recall-intensive performance and parity with transformer models, a direct efficient-attention/sequence-model contribution.

title: MoRA: Missing Modality Low-Rank Adaptation for Visual Recognition
topic: Low-rank missing-modality adaptation with efficient visual inference
why: The official abstract uses only 0.11 percent of full-fine-tuning trainable parameters and 25.90 percent of the inference time of the prior state of the art in missing-modality scenarios. This is a direct parameter- and inference-efficient method.

title: MOSS: Efficient and Accurate FP8 LLM Training with Microscaling and Automatic Scaling
topic: FP8 microscaling for LLM training throughput
why: The official abstract reports FP8 training of a 7B model at comparable performance to BF16 with up to 34% higher training throughput while avoiding costly dequantization and online scaling overhead.

title: Motion Prior Distillation in Time Reversal Sampling for Generative Inbetweening
topic: Inference-time distillation for time-reversal video sampling
why: The official abstract introduces inference-time motion-prior distillation and deliberately avoids denoising the end-conditioned path that causes ambiguity. This directly removes part of the sampling workload while improving temporal coherence.

title: MotionStream: Real-Time Video Generation with Interactive Motion Controls
why: The official abstract reports sub-second latency, up to 29 FPS on one GPU, and two-orders-of-magnitude faster generation via causal distillation, sliding-window attention, attention sinks, and KV-cache rolling. This is a direct high-impact video-generation acceleration result.

title: MT-DAO: Multi-Timescale Distributed Adaptive Optimizers with Local Updates
topic: Distributed LLM pretraining and communication efficiency
why: The first-party abstract reports 6%–27% lower iso-token wall-clock time and, at 720M scale, 24% fewer steps and 35% less time than DDP. This is a direct, quantified distributed-training efficiency contribution with convergence guarantees.

title: Much Ado About Noising: Dispelling the Myths of Generative Robotic Control
topic: Two-step iterative policy for efficient generative robotic control
why: The official abstract finds that a lightweight two-step regression policy essentially matches flow-based generative control policies, showing that expensive distribution fitting is not essential. This is a direct compute-reduction opportunity for protected Physical-AI action inference.

title: Multi-agent Coordination via Flow Matching
topic: One-step flow-policy distillation for fast multi-agent action inference
why: The official abstract distills flow-based joint behavior into decentralized one-step policies and reports about 14.5x faster inference than diffusion-based MARL while maintaining performance. This is a direct, quantified Physical-AI action-inference acceleration result.

title: Multi-Head Low-Rank Attention
why: ICLR 2026 Poster; partitionable low-rank latent states for TP decoding, reporting 2.8x decoding speedup over MLA.

title: Multi-Subspace Multi-Modal Modeling for Diffusion Models: Estimation, Convergence and Mixture of Experts
topic: Parameter-efficient multimodal diffusion with MoE latent modeling
why: The official abstract reports an MoE-latent model matching MoE U-Net performance with 10x fewer parameters and provides theoretical estimation/convergence analysis. This is a direct parameter-efficiency result for generative models.

title: Multi-View Encoders for Performance Prediction in LLM-Based Agentic Workflows
why: The official abstract uses a lightweight workflow predictor to avoid expensive trial-and-error evaluations of agent configurations. It directly reduces workflow evaluation overhead while preserving predictive utility.

title: Multimodal Policy Internalization for Conversational Agents
topic: Internalized multimodal policies for efficient agent inference
why: The official abstract internalizes long multimodal policies into model parameters so they need not be supplied in-context on every query, eliminating a fixed inference-time policy cost. This directly targets efficient conversational-agent deployment.

title: Muon Outperforms Adam in Tail-End Associative Memory Learning
why: The paper analyzes Muon's training advantage and relates it to associative-memory parameters and heavy-tailed data. The official abstract states Muon is consistently faster than Adam in LLM training and provides theoretical/empirical evidence explaining the mechanism, a direct training-efficiency result.

title: MuonBP: Faster Muon via Block-Periodic Orthogonalization
topic: Communication- and throughput-efficient distributed foundation-model training
why: The official abstract applies block-periodic orthogonalization to reduce model-parallel communication overhead and reports an 8 percent throughput increase for an 8B model without performance degradation. This is a direct distributed-training optimization.

title: MVAR: Visual Autoregressive Modeling with Scale and Spatial Markovian Conditioning
why: The official abstract reduces attention complexity from O(N^2) to O(Nk), removes the need for KV cache at inference, and reports 3.0x lower average GPU memory while training on eight RTX 4090s. This is a direct generation-efficiency contribution.

title: Nano3D: A Training-Free Approach for Efficient 3D Editing Without Masks
why: The official abstract explicitly describes a training-free approach for efficient 3D editing without masks. This is a concrete reduction in adaptation overhead for a generative 3D workflow and directly fits the efficient-generation landscape.

title: Natural Language PDDL (NL-PDDL) for Open-world Goal-oriented Commonsense Regression Planning in Embodied AI
topic: Lifted open-world planning with complexity independent of grounded objects/actions
why: The first-party abstract explicitly avoids exhaustive grounding and yields time/space complexity independent of the number of ground objects, states, and actions while improving embodied planning; this is a direct efficient-reasoning contribution.

title: Near-Optimal Online Deployment and Routing for Streaming LLMs
topic: LLM serving, model deployment, and cost-aware routing
why: The first-party abstract directly couples stage-wise model deployment with per-query routing under concurrency, throughput, and cost budgets, with near-optimal regret guarantees. This is a core LLM-serving systems contribution.

title: NEO — No-Optimization Test-Time Adaptation through Latent Re-Centering
topic: Low-overhead test-time adaptation and edge inference
why: The first-party abstract reports 63% lower inference time and 9% lower memory on Raspberry Pi and Jetson Orin Nano, while improving accuracy and using the least compute among compared TTA methods. This is a direct edge-inference efficiency result.

title: Neodragon: Mobile Video Generation Using Diffusion Transformer
topic: Low-power NPU video generation through distillation, pruning, and sampling-cost reduction
why: The official abstract targets mobile NPUs and combines encoder/decoder distillation, block pruning, and reduced diffusion sampling cost; it reports generating 49 frames at 640x1024 in 6.7 seconds on the target device. This is a direct deployment and measured efficiency result.

title: Neon: Negative Extrapolation From Self-Training Improves Image Generation
topic: Compute-efficient self-training correction for generative models
why: The official abstract reports a post-hoc weight merge requiring no new real data and typically less than 1% additional training compute; ImageNet 256×256 reaches FID 1.02 with only 0.36% additional compute. This is a direct, quantified training-efficiency result.

title: NeRV-Diffusion: Diffuse Implicit Neural Representation for Video Synthesis
topic: Implicit neural representation and sublinear-complexity video diffusion
why: The official abstract replaces frame-wise feature maps with compact generated neural weights, obviates temporal cross-frame attention, and states sublinear complexity overhead as resolution and video length increase. This is a direct video-generation efficiency contribution.

title: Neural Compression of 3D Meshes using Sparse Implicit Representation
why: The official abstract uses surface-local SDF grids and a lightweight compression network to reduce memory while preserving precise surface recovery, reporting improved compression and computational efficiency over prior mesh/point-cloud methods. This is a direct compression contribution.

title: Neural Dynamics Self-Attention for Spiking Transformers
why: The official abstract eliminates explicit attention-matrix storage through charge-fire-reset dynamics, reducing inference memory overhead while improving visual-task performance in energy-efficient SNNs.

title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection in Instruction Tuning for Large Language Models
why: The official abstract selects a 10% Alpaca-GPT4 subset using reusable neuron-activation features and reports it consistently outperforming larger-data selection baselines. This is direct, quality-gated instruction-tuning efficiency.

title: No outlier channels but with outlier blocks
why: NuBitQ introduces layer-specific arbitrary-bit non-uniform quantization and outlier compensation, avoiding costly Hessian computation and fine-tuning. The official abstract directly targets efficient LLM compression with hardware/deployment relevance.

title: Non-Convex Federated Optimization under Cost-Aware Client Selection
why: The first-party abstract explicitly models communication/local computation costs and achieves best-known complexities under cost-aware client selection using variance-reduced gradient estimation. This is direct federated-training efficiency.

title: Not All Documents Are What You Need for Extracting Instruction Tuning Data
why: The official abstract selects document clusters and high-quality QA pairs with a bandit strategy, reducing computational cost by 5–10x while improving accuracy by 2.5%. This is direct training-data generation efficiency.

title: OBS-Diff: Accurate Pruning For Diffusion Models in One-Shot
topic: Training-free structured and unstructured pruning for diffusion inference
why: The official abstract targets the prohibitive compute cost of text-to-image diffusion and introduces training-free one-shot pruning across unstructured, N:M, attention-head, and FFN granularities. This is a direct model-compression and inference-cost reduction method.

title: Octax: Accelerated CHIP-8 Arcade Environments for Reinforcement Learning in JAX
why: The first-party abstract reports orders-of-magnitude speedups over CPU emulators and improved RL training speed and scalability through end-to-end JAX/GPU environments. This is a direct training-infrastructure efficiency contribution.

title: OD$^3$: Optimization-free Dataset Distillation for Object Detection
topic: Compute-efficient object-detection training via dataset distillation
why: The official abstract reduces object-detection datasets to 0.25%–5% of their original size without optimization-based distillation and reports more than 14% mAP50 improvement over the prior method at 1% compression. This is a direct training-data efficiency result.

title: On Discriminative vs. Generative classifiers: Rethinking MLLMs for Action Understanding
topic: One-step discriminative action classification for efficient MLLM inference
why: The official abstract replaces autoregressive action-label generation with one-step discriminative classification and reports 3 times faster inference with an average 2.5 percent accuracy gain on the largest COIN benchmark. This is a direct efficient action-understanding method.

title: On the Design of One-step Diffusion via Shortcutting Flow Paths
why: The official abstract explicitly targets one-step diffusion by shortcutting flow paths. This directly reduces generation steps and is a core diffusion/flow acceleration contribution.

title: One Life to Learn: Inferring Symbolic World Models for Stochastic Environments from Unguided Exploration
topic: Sparse conditional symbolic computation for data-efficient world-model learning
why: The first-party abstract uses conditionally activated programmatic laws to route inference and optimization only through relevant dynamics, avoiding scaling with inactive rules and learning from minimal unguided interaction; this is a direct efficient-reasoning/agent contribution.

title: One-Step Flow for Image Super-Resolution with Tunable Fidelity-Realism Trade-offs
topic: One-step flow distillation for image super-resolution
why: The official abstract explicitly identifies the computational overhead of numerous sampling steps and distills a teacher flow model into a one-step student with tunable fidelity-realism. This directly reduces generation-step cost.

title: One-Step Flow Q-Learning: Addressing the Diffusion Policy Bottleneck in Offline Reinforcement Learning
topic: One-step flow action generation for offline RL and robotics
why: The official abstract reports one-step action generation during training and inference without auxiliary modules or distillation, substantially reducing computation and outperforming multi-step diffusion Q-learning; it is a protected Physical-AI result.

title: Online Pseudo-Zeroth-Order Training of Neuromorphic Spiking Neural Networks
why: OPZO replaces spatial backpropagation with a single forward pass, noise injection, and top-down signals, targeting on-chip SNN training. The official abstract reports competitive performance with spatial BP and estimated low training costs, directly relevant to energy-efficient neuromorphic learning.

title: OPRIDE: Efficient Offline Preference-based Reinforcement Learning via In-Dataset Exploration
why: The first-party abstract directly targets low query efficiency, uses informative in-dataset exploration, and reports strong performance with notably fewer human preference queries plus theoretical guarantees.

title: Optimal Aggregation of LLM and PRM Signals for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
why: The official abstract reports that calibrated signal aggregation improves test-time scaling efficiency while using only about 21.3% of the computation of the comparison approach. This is a direct, quantified inference-time efficiency result.

title: Optimal Brain Restoration for Joint Quantization and Sparsification of LLMs
topic: Joint LLM quantization and sparsity for inference acceleration
why: The official abstract reports W4A4KV4 with 50% sparsity and up to 4.72x speedup and 6.4x memory reduction over an FP16-dense baseline.

title: OrderDP: A Theoretically Guaranteed Lossless Dynamic Data Pruning Framework
topic: Lossless data pruning for training acceleration
why: The official abstract gives theoretical convergence/generalization guarantees and reports over 40% lower training cost with competitive accuracy on CIFAR and ImageNet. This is a direct, quantified efficient-training contribution.

title: OSCAR: Online Soft Compression for RAG
why: OSCAR performs query-dependent online soft compression of retrieved context, reducing long-context cost without offline storage overhead. The official abstract reports 2–5 times inference speedup with minimal or no accuracy loss across 1B–24B LLMs, a direct efficient-serving result.

title: Otters: An Energy-Efficient Spiking Transformer via Optical Time-to-First-Spike Encoding
topic: Hardware-software co-design for energy-efficient SNN transformers
why: The official abstract reports a fabricated optoelectronic synapse co-design and a measured 1.77x energy-efficiency improvement over leading SNNs on a commercial 22nm process.

title: Out of the Memory Barrier: A Highly Memory-Efficient Training System for LLMs with Million-Token Contexts
why: The official abstract describes constant activation-memory training, paged KV management, CPU offloading, and sparse attention to address million-token LLM training bottlenecks. This is a direct long-context/distributed training systems contribution.

title: Overcoming Joint Intractability with Lossless Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
why: The official abstract identifies verification as a speculative-decoding bottleneck and introduces a provably lossless hierarchical verification method that increases accepted tokens. This directly targets inference speed while preserving distribution fidelity.

title: Overthinking Reduction with Decoupled Rewards and Curriculum Data Scheduling
topic: token-efficient reasoning with decoupled rewards and curriculum scheduling
why: The official abstract directly targets redundant reasoning and reports over 50% fewer reasoning tokens across seven benchmarks while maintaining or improving performance. This is a strong, quantified efficient-reasoning contribution; promote strongly.

title: P3D: Highly Scalable 3D Neural Surrogates for Physics Simulations with Global Context
topic: Scalable neural surrogates for physics simulation
why: The official abstract explicitly targets highly scalable neural surrogates for physics simulations. This is a direct surrogate-model acceleration contribution for simulation workloads and Physical-AI training.

title: PairFlow: Closed-Form Source-Target Coupling for Few-Step Generation in Discrete Flow Models
topic: Few-step discrete-flow generation with low-cost training preprocessing
why: The official abstract directly targets slow iterative sampling and introduces a lightweight coupling/preprocessing method that uses up to 1.7% of full-training compute, matches or exceeds two-stage finetuning, and enables further distillation acceleration. This is a direct generation-efficiency result.

title: Pairwise is Not Enough: Hypergraph Neural Networks for Multi-Agent Pathfinding
topic: Compact hypergraph attention for efficient multi-agent pathfinding
why: The official abstract reports a 1M-parameter solver outperforming an 85M-parameter baseline trained on 100× more data, directly improving model/data efficiency while targeting online MAPF computation.

title: PALC: Preference Alignment via Logit Calibration
why: PALC aligns preferences through vocabulary-space logit calibration with a small bottleneck and no external reward model or guided decoding. The official abstract reports near-baseline inference speed and runtime adjustment without retraining, directly supporting resource-constrained LLM deployment.

title: Parallel Sampling from Masked Diffusion Models via Conditional Independence Testing
topic: Training-free parallel token sampling for masked diffusion
why: The official abstract introduces a model-agnostic sampler that identifies conditionally independent, high-confidence token groups for parallel unmasking and reports a better accuracy-compute trade-off. This directly addresses discrete-generation inference efficiency.

title: Parallel Token Prediction for  Language Models
topic: Multi-token prediction per forward pass for language-model decoding
why: The official abstract identifies one-token-per-pass autoregressive decoding as a latency bottleneck and proposes jointly predictable multiple tokens in a single model call. This is a direct decoding-architecture acceleration direction.

title: Parameter-Efficient Reinforcement Learning using Prefix Optimization
why: The first-party abstract optimizes only a short prefix and generates the rest from the reference model, reporting substantial gains for a tiny fraction of standard RL compute. This is a direct, quantified efficient-reasoning training contribution.

title: ParaRNN: Unlocking Parallel Training of Nonlinear RNNs for Large Language Models
topic: parallel training of nonlinear recurrent LLMs
why: The official abstract reports up to 665x speedup over naive sequential nonlinear-RNN training and demonstrates 7B-scale LSTM/GRU models. This is a direct training-parallelism result.

title: PARD: Accelerating LLM Inference with Low‑Cost PARallel Draft Model Adaptation
why: The official abstract identifies memory-bandwidth-limited autoregressive decoding and per-target draft-head adaptation cost, then proposes a reusable draft model with parallel token prediction. This directly targets LLM inference latency and adaptation overhead.

title: ParoQuant: Pairwise Rotation Quantization for Efficient Reasoning LLM Inference
topic: LLM quantization; reasoning inference; rotation quantization; weight-only PTQ; GPU kernels
why: UCSD Z Lab / MIT Han Lab true canonical miss found on fresh recheck: ICLR 2026 weight-only PTQ combines optimizable pairwise Givens rotations with channel scaling and a co-designed inference kernel, improving reasoning-model quantization accuracy with lightweight runtime overhead.

title: Partition Generative Modeling: Masked Modeling Without Masks
topic: Mask-free parallel generation with reduced sampling work
why: The official abstract removes uninformative mask tokens so sampling processes only clean tokens while retaining parallel any-order generation, reporting 5–5.5x throughput on text and 7.5x on ImageNet versus relevant masked-generation baselines. This is a directly measured inference-efficiency result.

title: PASER: Post-Training Data Selection for Efficient Pruned Large Language Model Recovery
why: PASER adaptively selects capability-specific recovery instructions and filters conflicting samples. The official abstract reports recovery using only 4–20 percent of the original post-training data, a direct training-efficiency result for compressed LLMs.

title: Pay Attention to CTC: Fast and Robust Pseudo-Labelling for Unified Speech Recognition
topic: Training-time pseudo-labeling acceleration for speech models
why: The official abstract replaces costly autoregressive pseudo-labeling and beam search with CTC-driven teacher forcing and simultaneous decoder targets, reporting a 50% reduction in training time with improved robustness and accuracy.

title: PCLR: Progressively Compressed LoRA for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
why: The first-party abstract compresses and integrates LoRA branches to control memory explosion while preserving continual-learning performance, reaching a memory budget close to non-extension methods. This is direct parameter/memory efficiency.

title: PEAR: Phase Entropy Aware Reward for Efficient Reasoning
why: The first-party abstract directly targets redundant long chain-of-thought traces that inflate inference cost. Its phase-dependent entropy reward reduces response length while maintaining competitive accuracy across six benchmarks and model scales, making it a strong efficient-reasoning result.

title: PEERING INTO THE UNKNOWN: ACTIVE VIEW SELECTION WITH NEURAL UNCERTAINTY MAPS FOR 3D RECONSTRUCTION
topic: Low-cost active view selection for 3D reconstruction

title: PerFit: Exploring Personalization Shifts in Representation Space of LLMs
why: The official abstract reports an average 92.3% reduction in parameter count versus the state-of-the-art personalization method while retaining strong performance. This is a direct, quantified parameter-efficiency contribution.

title: PhaseFormer: From Patches to Phases for Efficient and Effective Time Series Forecasting
why: PhaseFormer replaces inefficient patch-level processing with phase-wise prediction and lightweight routing, achieving benchmark-leading forecasting with around 1k parameters. This is a direct compact-model efficiency result

title: PHAT: Modeling Period Heterogeneity for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

title: Photon: Speedup Volume Understanding with Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

why: The official abstract describes adaptive token reduction during training and inference and reports lower resource use and faster inference at state-of-the-art accuracy for 3D medical VQA.

title: pi-Flow: Policy-Based Few-Step Generation via Imitation Distillation
topic: Few-step flow inference acceleration for large image-generation models
why: The first-party abstract explicitly replaces additional network evaluations with a network-free policy, reports 1-NFE FID 2.85, and improves diversity at 4 NFEs on FLUX.1-12B and Qwen-Image-20B while maintaining teacher-level quality; this is direct, high-value inference acceleration.

title: Pinet: Optimizing hard-constrained neural networks with orthogonal projection layers
why: The official abstract uses projection layers to solve constrained optimization faster than traditional solvers, especially for batches, and reports orders-of-magnitude advantages over learning approaches in training time and solution quality. title: Pixel to Gaussian: Ultra-Fast Continuous Super-Resolution with 2D Gaussian Modeling
topic: Continuous super-resolution acceleration via Gaussian rendering

topic: Adaptive token-budget allocation for efficient LLM reasoning
why: The official abstract adaptively allocates reasoning tokens by sub-question complexity and reports 39 percent token reduction, up to 70 percent accuracy gains, and improved efficiency metrics without retraining. This directly addresses overthinking and compute-optimal inference.

title: Planned Diffusion
topic: parallel and planned decoding for diffusion language-model inference
why: The official abstract describes a model-generated denoising order that partitions responses into semantically independent chunks and then generates chunks in parallel. It directly targets the latency-versus-quality trade-off in discrete diffusion LLM decoding.

title: PM-KVQ: Progressive Mixed-precision KV Cache Quantization for Long-CoT LLMs
topic: progressive KV-cache quantization for long reasoning contexts
why: The official abstract identifies cumulative quantization error and short-context calibration failures in long-CoT decoding, then introduces progressive mixed-precision KV-cache quantization. This directly addresses inference memory and quality-efficiency trade-offs.

title: PolySkill: Learning Generalizable Skills Through Polymorphic Abstraction For Continual Learning
topic: reusable skills for step-efficient LLM agents
why: The official abstract reports 1.7x improved skill reuse, up to 9.4/13.9% success gains, and over 20% fewer steps by separating abstract goals from concrete execution. This is a direct, measured agent-execution efficiency contribution; promote strongly.

title: Post-Training Quantization for Video Matting
why: The official abstract presents a task-specific PTQ framework with temporal optical-flow guidance and near-full-precision performance under ultra-low-bit quantization, directly addressing deployment cost.

title: PPE: Positional Preservation Embedding for Token Compression in Multimodal Large Language Models
topic: Position-preserving visual-token compression for efficient MLLM inference
why: The official abstract provides a parameter-free positional encoding operator that improves cascade visual-token compression while preserving spatiotemporal structure, yielding 2 to 5 percent benchmark gains. It directly supports efficient multimodal token reduction.

title: PPLLaVA: Varied Video Sequence Understanding With Prompt Guidance
why: The official abstract directly targets redundant video content through instruction-aware token compression and reports superior throughput while handling seconds-to-hours videos. This is a core multimodal inference-efficiency contribution.

title: PQGAN: Product-Quantised Image Representation for High-Quality Image Synthesis
topic: Product-quantized image representations for efficient synthesis
why: The official abstract directly introduces product-quantized image representations for synthesis. This is a core compression and efficient-generation contribution with a clear path to reduced representation cost.

title: Pre-training under infinite compute
why: The first-party abstract reports a 5.17x data-efficiency improvement in the loss asymptote, 9% better pretraining evaluations, and an 8x smaller distilled student retaining 83% of the ensemble benefit. This is a direct, quantified pretraining-efficiency result.

title: PreciseCache: Precise Feature Caching for Efficient and High-fidelity Video Generation
topic: feature caching for video diffusion inference
why: The official abstract identifies redundant feature computation across video diffusion steps and introduces precise caching with quality-aware reuse. This directly targets video-generation inference efficiency.

title: Predicting LLM Output Length via Entropy-Guided Representations
topic: Length-aware LLM serving and batched-inference throughput
why: The official abstract targets padding waste in LLM serving and RL sampling, reuses hidden states for near-zero-cost length prediction, and reports end-to-end throughput gains with a length-aware scheduler. This is a direct serving-efficiency contribution.

title: Predicting LLM Reasoning Performance with Small Proxy Model
why: The official abstract reports over 100x lower dataset-ranking cost using sub-1B proxy models while predicting reasoning performance across 1B–32B models. This is a direct, quantified reduction in expensive model-development evaluation.

why: The official abstract reports a 160M-parameter LM plus 18M memory matching a model with more than 2× the parameters while using a hierarchical memory bank, directly improving model-size and inference-memory efficiency.

title: Prompt Curriculum Learning for Efficient LLM Post-Training

why: The official abstract avoids costly rollout filtering and reports 12.1x/16.9x faster identification of informative prompts plus less training time to reach comparable performance. This is direct RL post-training efficiency.

topic: Proof-length and verification-cost reduction for reasoning LMs
why: The official abstract reduces proof length by 87 percent on miniF2F and also speeds Lean checking, while simplifying long RL-generated proofs without human demonstrations. This directly reduces downstream reasoning and verification cost.

title: PROS: Towards Compute-Efficient RLVR via Rollout Prefix Reuse
topic: RLVR rollout prefix reuse and compute reduction

title: ProtoKV: Long-context Knowledges Are Already Well-Organized Before Your Query
why: ProtoKV clusters semantic-anchor and position-determined tokens into compression units for KV-cache retention. The official abstract reports 2.11 percentage points higher LongBench accuracy than state-of-the-art methods at matched memory constraints, directly targeting long-context memory efficiency.

title: ProxyAttn: Guided Sparse Attention via Representative Heads
why: ICLR 2026 Poster; representative-head token-level sparse attention, reporting up to 10.3x attention and 2.4x prefill acceleration.

why: PruneSID dynamically compresses redundant visual tokens while preserving importance and diversity. The official abstract reports 96.3 percent LLaVA-1.5 accuracy at 11.1 percent token retention and 7.8 times faster prefilling, a direct MLLM inference-efficiency result.

topic: Cost-aware layer pruning for LLM inference
why: The official abstract directly targets LLM inference cost and proposes surrogate-assisted Shapley estimation plus stratified mask sampling to make layer-pruning decisions at lower computational cost. This is a direct model-compression and deployment-efficiency contribution.

title: Pruning Long Chain-of-Thought of Large Reasoning Models via Small-Scale Preference Optimization
topic: Length-controlled preference optimization for efficient reasoning
why: The official abstract reports over 50% lower average reasoning-output length across multiple benchmarks while maintaining reasoning performance, using limited tuning data and training. This is a direct, quantified inference-cost reduction.

title: PT$^2$-LLM: Post-Training Ternarization for Large Language Models
why: PT²-LLM directly targets LLM memory and compute demands through training-free post-training ternarization and refinement. This is a hardware/deployment-oriented quantization method and qualifies as a strong efficient-ML record.

title: PTQ4ARVG: Post-Training Quantization for AutoRegressive Visual Generation Models
topic: Training-free quantization for autoregressive visual generation
why: The official abstract targets model size and computational latency in autoregressive visual generation and introduces a training-free PTQ framework for channel outliers, dynamic token activations, and sample distributions. This is a direct deployment and inference-efficiency contribution.

title: Pyramid Patchification Flow for Visual Generation
topic: Timestep-adaptive patchification for diffusion sampling efficiency
why: The official abstract reduces token counts at high-noise timesteps using larger patches and reports 2.02x denoising speedup with image quality retained, while requiring only 8.9% additional training FLOPs from pretrained SiT-XL/2. This is a directly quantified diffusion-inference acceleration method.

title: Q&C: When Quantization Meets Cache in Efficient Generation
topic: joint quantization and cache acceleration for generation
why: The official abstract studies the interaction between quantization and caching and proposes a hybrid acceleration method to address calibration and error accumulation. This is directly relevant to generation-time efficiency.

title: Q-RAG: Long Context Multi‑Step Retrieval via Value‑Based Embedder Training
topic: Resource-efficient multi-step retrieval for long-context LLMs
why: The official abstract trains an embedder rather than a small LLM for multi-step retrieval and reports state-of-the-art results up to 10M-token contexts as a resource-efficient alternative. This directly reduces retrieval and inference burden.

why: PAMM compresses Q/K/V projection activations by up to 512 times while maintaining similar or better perplexity and composes with FlashAttention. This is a direct memory-efficiency method for LLM training.

topic: Two-bit post-training quantization for diffusion LLMs

why: The official abstract reports 4-bit QuantVGGT achieving 3.7x memory reduction and 2.5x real-hardware inference acceleration while preserving over 98% reconstruction quality.

topic: joint quantization and sparse attention for video diffusion
why: The official abstract describes a unified quantization+sparsification method for HunyuanVideo-13B to address high compute/memory cost and compression-induced quality loss. This is a direct diffusion deployment/acceleration contribution.

why: The official abstract estimates answerability before generating tokens and enables adaptive RAG, cascading, or abstention, thereby reducing inference costs while preserving performance. This is a direct compute-allocation method.

topic: Query-aware token pruning for streaming video understanding
why: The official abstract introduces a lightweight, training-free pruning and response-scheduling module that matches full-token baselines while pruning over 70% of visual tokens. This is a direct efficient streaming-inference contribution with a clear compute-reduction mechanism.

why: The official abstract directly routes queries across model sizes and reasoning budgets to balance performance, cost, and latency. It provides a lightweight, interpretable deployment method for efficient reasoning.

why: The official abstract stores compact key-value knowledge with cost independent of task volume and supports order-agnostic insertion/removal without retraining. This directly improves continual adaptation efficiency.
