title: SafeFlowMatcher: Safe and Fast Planning using Flow Matching with Control Barrier Functions
topic: real-time flow-matching planning for Physical AI
why: The official abstract combines a one-or-few-step flow-matching predictor with a barrier-function correction to achieve real-time planning with safety guarantees. This directly concerns action-generation latency and runtime.

title: Sample More to Think Less: Group Filtered Policy Optimization for Concise Reasoning
topic: Training concise reasoning to reduce LLM inference tokens and latency
why: The official abstract reports up to 85% reduction in GRPO length inflation while preserving accuracy, with only 7% additional training time and about 30% end-to-end latency reduction. This is a direct LLM inference-cost and serving-latency result.

title: Sample Reward Soups: Query-efficient Multi-Reward Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
why: The official abstract states that multi-reward alignment can require exponentially many reward queries and proposes an inference-time soup strategy. The method directly addresses query and guidance efficiency.

title: SAQ: Stabilizer-Aware Quantum Error Correction Decoder
why: SAQ-Decoder combines a transformer with constraint-aware post-processing and achieves near-maximum-likelihood accuracy with linear computational scalability and parameter efficiency. It directly addresses the accuracy/complexity tradeoff in practical learned decoding.

title: Scalable Chain of Thoughts via Elastic Reasoning
why: The first-party abstract directly addresses token, latency, and compute budgets and reports more concise reasoning plus significantly lower training cost with robust truncated-budget behavior. This is a core efficient-reasoning contribution.

title: Scalable Multi-Task Low-Rank Model Adaptation
why: The official abstract reports 47% fewer parameters and 24% less training time while improving average accuracy by 2.3 points across 15–25 tasks. This is a direct, quantified adaptation-efficiency contribution.

title: Scale-wise Distillation of Diffusion Models
topic: Progressive scale-wise distillation for few-step image/video generation
why: The official abstract avoids redundant intermediate-timestep computation through progressive generation and reports sampling speed approaching two full-resolution steps under matched compute budgets. This is a direct diffusion inference-efficiency method.

title: Scaling Attention via Feature Sparsity
topic: efficient attention / feature sparsity / FlashSFA kernel
why: ICLR 2026 introduces Sparse Feature Attention and FlashSFA; reports up to 2.5x speedup and nearly 50% FLOP/KV-cache reduction while matching dense baselines.

title: Scaling Large Vision-Language Model RL Training via Efficient Load Balancing
why: Official ICLR 2026 paper reports up to 8.47x end-to-end throughput on 128 GPU multimodal RL; system-level first-party verified true miss.

title: Scaling Laws Meet Model Architecture: Toward Inference-Efficient LLMs
topic: architecture-aware inference cost scaling for LLMs
why: The official abstract studies hidden size, MLP/attention allocation, and GQA under accuracy/inference-cost trade-offs and introduces conditional scaling laws plus architecture search. This directly informs inference-efficient model architecture selection.

title: Scaling Speech Tokenizers with Diffusion Autoencoders
topic: Low-rate, low-bit-rate speech representation for speech-language models
why: The official abstract reports a diffusion tokenizer operating at 12.5 Hz and 200 bits per second while supporting high-fidelity audio reconstruction and strong understanding/generation. This is a directly quantified representation and token-rate efficiency contribution.

title: Scaling up Memory for Robotic Control via Experience Retrieval
why: The official abstract identifies the compute and brittleness cost of conditioning on long observation histories and proposes selecting task-relevant keyframes for a hierarchical VLA policy. It directly reduces the history burden in Physical-AI inference.

title: Scaling with Collapse: Efficient and Predictable Training of LLM Families
topic: Compute-efficient LLM training and early stopping
why: The first-party abstract links loss-curve collapse to compute-efficient training and demonstrates early diagnostics and early stopping for large-scale tuning. It also trains a competitive LLM family, making this a direct training-efficiency contribution.

title: ScalingCache: Extreme Acceleration of DiTs through Difference Scaling and Dynamic Interval Caching
topic: Training-free activation caching for diffusion-transformer inference
why: The official abstract reports approximately 2.5x acceleration for Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo and 3.1x for FLUX with near-lossless quality, directly matching generation acceleration.

title: SCOPED: Score–Curvature Out-of-distribution Proximity Evaluator for Diffusion
why: The official abstract reports an order-of-magnitude reduction in diffusion-model forward passes for OOD detection while retaining competitive accuracy. The reduction in model evaluations is a direct inference-efficiency claim.

title: Score Distillation Beyond Acceleration: Generative Modeling from Corrupted Data
why: The official abstract reports a one-step generator with up to 30x speedup over multi-step diffusion while improving FID across noisy generation, restoration, and MRI tasks.

title: SCRIBES: Web-Scale Script-Based Semi-Structured Data Extraction with Reinforcement Learning
topic: Reusable-script extraction for resource-efficient LLM data pipelines
why: The official abstract replaces per-page LLM inference with reusable extraction scripts and reports over 13 percent higher script quality and more than 4 percent downstream QA accuracy gain. This directly improves web-scale extraction efficiency.

title: Secure Outlier-Aware Large Language Model Inference
topic: Secure MPC LLM inference nonlinear-operation acceleration
why: The official abstract reports nearly 2x RMSNorm, 2x SiLU, and over 5x Softmax acceleration in secure LLM inference without fine-tuning, directly addressing cryptographic inference latency.

title: SeedVR2: One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training
why: The official abstract targets prohibitive high-resolution video-restoration inference cost and demonstrates comparable or better restoration quality in a single diffusion step.

title: Seesaw: Accelerating Training by Balancing Batch Size and Learning Rate Scheduling
why: The official abstract derives a batch-ramp schedule and reports about 36 percent lower wall-clock time at equal FLOPs on 150M to 600M models. This is a direct, quantified training-efficiency contribution.

title: Segment Any Events with Language
why: The first-party abstract reports superior inference speed with a parameter-efficient architecture for open-vocabulary event segmentation and a prompt-free variant. This is a direct efficient multimodal inference contribution.

title: Segment-Level Attribution for Selective Learning of Long Reasoning Traces
why: The first-party abstract directly targets repetitive and uninformative CoT segments. Attribution-guided selective SFT masks low-value segments and reports improved accuracy and output efficiency across models and datasets, making it a strong efficient-reasoning result.

title: Selective Rotary Position Embedding
topic: Selective RoPE for efficient gated linear attention
why: Selective RoPE adds input-dependent rotations to gated linear attention with minimal architectural overhead and an efficient recurrent implementation. The official abstract reports improved recall, accuracy, and expressivity on synthetic tasks and 370M-parameter LM pretraining, directly advancing efficient sequence modeling.

title: Self-Aligned Reward: Towards Effective and Efficient Reasoners
topic: Concise reasoning and efficient LLM reinforcement learning
why: The official abstract introduces a self-aligned reward and reports 30 percent shorter answers with 4 percent higher accuracy across models and benchmarks. It directly reduces reasoning-token and inference cost.

title: Self-Forcing++: Towards Minute-Scale High-Quality Video Generation
topic: Long-horizon video generation acceleration and diffusion efficiency
why: The official abstract identifies prohibitive long-video compute and avoids recomputing overlapping frames while using self-generated segments to guide the student. It scales generation to 4 minutes 15 seconds and up to 20 times the teacher horizon, making it a direct efficiency contribution for video generation.

title: Self-Speculative Decoding Accelerates Lossless Inference in Any-Order and Any-Subset Autoregressive Models
topic: lossless speculative decoding for nonstandard autoregressive models
why: The official abstract describes Any-Subset Speculative Decoding for parallel token generation with distribution correction, directly addressing lossless inference acceleration rather than only output quality.

title: Self-Speculative Masked Diffusions
topic: Speculative decoding and reduced function evaluations for masked diffusion
why: The first-party abstract explicitly introduces model-integrated draft generation and parallel validation, reporting approximately 2x fewer network forward passes than standard masked diffusion. This is a direct and quantified generative-inference acceleration contribution.

title: Semantic Parallelism: Redefining Efficient MoE Inference via Model-Data Co-Scheduling
topic: MoE systems / expert parallelism / serving / communication
why: ICLR 2026 Sem-MoE co-schedules expert placement and request/token placement inside SGLang to reduce expert-parallel all-to-all communication and improve inference throughput.

title: Semantic Voting: A Self-Evaluation-Free Approach for Efficient LLM Self-Improvement on Unverifiable Open-ended Tasks
why: The first-party abstract directly removes high-overhead LLM self-evaluation from self-improvement, replacing it with lightweight semantic voting. It reports substantial computational-efficiency gains and better performance across architectures/tasks.

title: Sequential Parallel Duality in Prefix Scannable Models
topic: Linear-time sequence models and parallel-prefix inference
why: The official abstract characterizes state-space and prefix-scannable sequence models that support parallel prefix evaluation together with linear-time, constant-space sequential inference. This is a direct algorithmic efficient-ML contribution with clear complexity guarantees.

title: SERE: Similarity-based Expert Re-routing for Efficient Batch Decoding in MoE Models
topic: MoE batch-decoding and expert activation efficiency
why: The official abstract describes input-aware expert rerouting to reduce active experts during memory-bound batch decoding while preserving critical experts. This directly targets MoE serving throughput and latency.

title: SHE-LoRA: Selective Homomorphic Encryption for Federated Tuning with Heterogeneous LoRA
topic: Communication- and encryption-efficient private federated LLM tuning
why: The official abstract selectively encrypts sensitive parameters and reports 99.71 percent lower communication overhead and 99.87 percent lower encryption time versus HE baselines while maintaining performance. This is a direct private-training systems result.

title: Shortcut Diffusion Training with Cumulative Consistency Loss: An Optimal Control View
topic: Few-step diffusion/flow generation via cumulative consistency training
why: The official abstract directly targets hundreds of denoising steps and proposes cumulative consistency loss to support larger step sizes while preserving quality. This is a direct generative-inference acceleration direction.

title: SigLIP-HD by Fine-to-Coarse Supervision
topic: Higher-resolution visual perception at fixed MLLM inference budget
why: The official abstract improves fine visual perception by supervising lower-resolution features from higher-resolution targets and produces better visual tokens at exactly the same inference budget. This directly improves VLM efficiency-quality trade-offs.

title: SIM-CoT: Supervised Implicit Chain-of-Thought
why: The official abstract stabilizes implicit reasoning and reports 2.3 times greater token efficiency than explicit CoT while surpassing its accuracy on GPT-2. The auxiliary decoder is removed at inference, preserving the efficiency benefit.

title: SketchThinker-R1: Towards Efficient Sketch-Style Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models
why: The official abstract reports over 64% reduction in reasoning-token cost without compromising final-answer accuracy. This is a direct, quantified multimodal inference-efficiency contribution.

title: SliderQuant: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
why: The official abstract directly studies challenging low-bit LLM post-training quantization and motivates layer-dependent quantization from measured sensitivity differences. This is a core model-compression contribution for efficient deployment.

title: Slow-Fast Policy Optimization: Reposition-Before-Update for LLM Reasoning
why: SFPO reports up to 4.93x fewer rollouts and 4.19x lower wall-clock time to match GRPO accuracy while improving reasoning scores. This is a direct, quantified training-efficiency result

title: Small Drafts, Big Verdict: Information-Intensive Visual Reasoning via Speculation
topic: Speculative decoding for information-intensive VLM reasoning
why: The official abstract combines lightweight VLM draft experts with a larger verdict model and explicitly aims to minimize computational cost while preserving reasoning accuracy. This is a direct speculative-inference optimization for multimodal models.

title: SmartChunk Retrieval: Query-Aware Chunk Compression with Planning for Efficient Document RAG
why: The first-party abstract uses a lightweight compression module and query-aware chunk planning to avoid static chunking and reduce RAG cost, while outperforming baselines across in- and out-of-domain QA. This is direct retrieval/inference efficiency.

title: SMixer: Rethinking Efficient-Training and Event-Driven SNNs
topic: Event-driven spiking-model architecture and training pruning
why: The official abstract combines asynchronous-friendly SNN architecture with trainable-parameter-free spatial-temporal spike pruning to reduce GPU training overhead while retaining competitive performance.

title: Smooth Reading: Bridging the Gap of Recurrent LLM to Self-Attention LLM on Long-Context Understanding
topic: Incremental recurrent-LLM inference for long context
why: The official abstract reports 2.5x faster training and 2x faster inference at 64K context while improving LongBench performance over self-attention baselines.

title: SNAP-UQ: Self-supervised Next-Activation Prediction for Single-Pass Uncertainty in TinyML
topic: Single-pass resource-efficient uncertainty monitoring for TinyML
why: The official abstract provides state-free single-pass uncertainty estimation with tiny int8 heads and reports roughly 40–60% smaller flash footprint and 25–35% faster latency than early-exit/ensemble baselines. This is a direct, quantified edge/TinyML efficiency contribution.

title: Soft-Di[M]O: Improving One-Step Discrete Image Generation with Soft Embeddings
why: The official abstract starts from one-step generators that compress multiple sampling steps into a single forward pass and introduces soft embeddings to enable end-to-end refinement. This directly supports efficient one-step image synthesis and post-distillation optimization.

title: SoLoPO: Unlocking Long-Context Capabilities in LLMs via Short-to-Long Preference Optimization
topic: Compute- and memory-efficient long-context LLM alignment
why: The official abstract decouples long-context preference optimization into short-context alignment and reward consistency and reports improvements in computational and memory efficiency. This directly improves long-context training scalability.

title: Solving Football by Exploiting Equilibrium Structure of 2p0s Differential Games with One-Sided Information
why: The paper collapses game-tree complexity from U-based growth to I-based action prototypes under its assumptions and reports improved learning efficiency. This is a direct algorithmic scalability contribution

title: SP-VLA: A Joint Model Scheduling and Token Pruning Approach for VLA Model Acceleration
topic: VLA runtime scheduling and token pruning
why: The official abstract identifies low VLA execution frequency and temporal/spatial redundancy, then jointly schedules a VLA model and lightweight generator while pruning visual tokens. This directly targets real-time embodied inference.

title: SpareTrain: Fault-Tolerant LLM Training via Low-Cost Dual Modular Redundancy
why: The official abstract repurposes activation checkpointing and idle GPU time to make full DMR practical, achieving only 3–14% overhead versus unprotected training. This directly improves training-system efficiency.

title: Sparse Attention Adaptation for Long Reasoning
topic: efficient attention / long reasoning / sparse decode / GPU kernel
why: SeerAttention-R adapts learned sparse attention to autoregressive reasoning decode; official ICLR paper reports up to about 9x sparse decoding kernel speedup over FlashAttention-3 at 90% sparsity.

title: Sparse Imagination for Efficient Visual World Model Planning
topic: sparse visual world-model rollouts for Physical AI planning
why: The official abstract explicitly reduces tokens processed during visual world-model forward prediction and latent rollouts using randomized grouped attention, accelerating planning under constrained robotics resources. This is a direct protected Physical-AI compute-efficiency contribution.

title: SparseD: Sparse Attention for Diffusion Language Models
topic: diffusion language model / sparse attention / inference acceleration
why: ICLR 2026 sparse-attention acceleration for diffusion language models; official paper reports up to 1.50x speedup at 64k context with 1,024 denoising steps.

title: Sparsity Forcing: Reinforcing Token Sparsity of MLLMs
topic: multimodal/MLLM efficiency / token sparsity / RL post-training
why: ICLR 2026 MLLM token-sparsity post-training framework; official paper reports token reduction up to 75%, inference memory reduction up to 3x and decode speedup up to 3.3x.

title: SpecBranch: Speculative Decoding via Hybrid Drafting and Rollback-Aware Branch Parallelism
why: The official abstract identifies serialized draft/target execution and waiting bubbles in speculative decoding, then uses branch parallelism with rollback-aware execution. This directly targets LLM decoding latency.

title: Spectral Attention Steering for Prompt Highlighting
why: The official abstract reports a training-free key-embedding steering method with substantially lower latency and memory overhead than attention-matrix-based steering, remaining compatible with optimized attention.

title: SpectralGCD: Spectral Concept Selection and Cross-modal Representation Learning for Generalized Category Discovery
why: SpectralGCD reports accuracy comparable or superior to state of the art at a fraction of the computational cost by using unified CLIP concept representations, spectral filtering, and distillation. This is a direct efficiency result

title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster AI Agents
topic: Lossless speculative execution for interactive agent runtime
why: The official abstract proposes parallel speculative future actions with commit-on-match semantics and reports up to 55% next-action prediction accuracy translating into substantial latency reduction across interactive domains. This is a direct agent-runtime acceleration result.

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding
why: ICLR 2026 direct speculative-decoding systems/algorithm result. Saguaro overlaps speculation with verification and reports up to 2x over optimized speculative decoding and 5x over autoregressive decoding.

title: Splat the Net: Radiance Fields with Splattable Neural Primitives
why: The official abstract avoids costly ray marching and matches 3DGS quality/speed while using 10x fewer primitives and 6x fewer parameters. This is a direct, quantified efficient 3D representation/rendering contribution.

title: SPRINT: Sparse-Dense Residual Fusion for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
topic: token dropping and sparse-dense fusion for DiT training
why: The official abstract identifies quadratic DiT training cost and enables up to 75% token dropping through shallow dense/deep sparse residual fusion with a short full-token fine-tuning stage. This is a direct generative-model compute-efficiency contribution.

title: Squeeze the Soaked Sponge: Efficient Off-policy RFT for Large Language Model
topic: off-policy rollout reuse for reasoning RL training
why: The official abstract reuses historical policy data for rollout-efficient RFT and reports 30x–450x reductions in rollout-data training cost versus recent models. This is direct compute/training efficiency.

title: SSVPO: Effective Step-Level Credit Assignment for RL Training of Language Models
topic: step-level credit assignment and reasoning-token reduction
why: The first-party abstract reports up to 11.6% accuracy gain, 18.1% fewer tokens, and 1.6x reasoning-efficiency improvement through Shapley-based step credit assignment. This is direct reasoning-training and inference efficiency.

title: ST-SimDiff: Balancing Spatiotemporal Similarity and Difference for Efficient Video Understanding with MLLMs
topic: Training-free spatiotemporal token reduction for video MLLMs
why: ST-SimDiff jointly retains representative static content and temporal change points with a training-free dual-selection strategy. The official abstract reports substantial computational-cost reduction while improving over prior methods, directly targeting efficient video-MLLM inference.

title: Stabilizing Policy Gradients for Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning in LLM Reasoning
why: CAPO masks unstable policy-gradient samples and reports up to 30x improved sample efficiency over standard GRPO while rejecting fewer than 8% of tokens. This is a direct, quantified LLM post-training efficiency result

title: Stacked from One: Multi-Scale Self-Injection for Context Window Extension
topic: Context compression and query-aware retrieval for long-context LLMs
why: The official abstract describes a compressor-decoder design that transfers context only at selected lower layers to reduce redundant computation, together with multi-grained context encoding and retrieval. This directly targets long-context model efficiency.

title: STARK: Strategic Team of Agents for Refining Kernels
topic: Multi-agent LLM framework for GPU kernel optimization
why: The official abstract directly targets labor-intensive GPU kernel optimization, uses profiling-feedback-driven multi-agent search, and reports kernels up to 16x faster than baseline implementations. This is a direct kernel/compiler optimization contribution.

title: STDDN: A Physics-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Crowd Simulation
why: The official abstract identifies inference inefficiency and high computational overhead in learned crowd simulation and reports a major reduction in inference latency with improved long-horizon accuracy. This directly targets efficient simulation.

title: STITCH: Simultaneous Thinking and Talking with Chunked Reasoning for Spoken Language Models
topic: streaming speech reasoning with latency hiding
why: The first-party abstract interleaves unspoken reasoning chunks with spoken output, hiding reasoning time behind audio playback. It matches baseline latency while improving math reasoning by 15%, directly improving latency/quality.

title: Stop Unnecessary Reflection: Training LRMs for Efficient Reasoning with Adaptive Reflection and Length Coordinated Penalty
topic: Adaptive reasoning-length reduction for LLM serving
why: The official abstract reports 53.1% fewer response tokens with 5.8% higher accuracy for a 1.5B reasoning model, directly reducing inference token cost and latency.

title: Stop Wasting Your Tokens: Towards Efficient Runtime Multi-Agent Systems
topic: LLM-free runtime supervision for token-efficient agents
why: The official abstract reports a 29.68% reduction in token consumption on GAIA without compromising success, using lightweight runtime supervision and context filtering. This is a direct, quantified agent-runtime efficiency contribution.

title: Stopping Computation for Converged Tokens in Masked Diffusion-LM Decoding
topic: token-level compute skipping in masked diffusion LLMs
why: The official abstract describes repeated attention and feed-forward recomputation for already-converged token positions and proposes locking stable tokens to skip projections and FFN work. This is a direct decoding-compute optimization.

title: STream3R: Scalable Sequential 3D Reconstruction with Causal Transformer
why: STream3R replaces expensive global optimization and poorly scaling memory with a causal streaming transformer for sequential 3D reconstruction. The official abstract emphasizes efficient online processing and scalable training, directly relevant to 3D/Physical-AI inference.

title: Streaming Autoregressive Video Generation via Diagonal Distillation
topic: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion for real-time streaming
why: The official abstract directly targets the latency-quality trade-off in real-time streaming video and introduces diagonal distillation to exploit temporal context while reducing denoising steps. This is a direct video-generation inference acceleration contribution.

title: Streaming Visual Geometry Transformer
topic: Low-latency streaming geometry with temporal KV caching
why: The official abstract explicitly targets interactive low-latency 3D reconstruction and uses causal attention with cached historical keys and values for efficient online processing. This is a direct streaming and cache-reuse contribution.

title: StreamingThinker: Large Language Models Can Think While Reading
topic: Streaming reasoning and parallel inference for LLMs
why: The official abstract identifies unnecessary latency from waiting for the full input and introduces streaming chain-of-thought generation, streaming-constrained training, and streaming parallel inference. This directly addresses latency in dynamic LLM workloads.

title: StreamSplat: Towards Online Dynamic 3D Reconstruction from Uncalibrated Video Streams
why: The official abstract replaces hours of per-scene optimization with feed-forward online reconstruction and reports a 1200x speedup for arbitrarily long video streams. This is a direct, quantified real-time reconstruction acceleration result.

title: Study of Training Dynamics for Memory-Constrained Fine-Tuning
topic: Dynamic channel sparsity for memory-constrained fine-tuning
why: The official abstract introduces dynamic channel selection for fine-tuning under strict memory constraints and reports very high activation and weight-derivative sparsity. This is a direct training-efficiency and resource-constrained optimization contribution.

title: SURGE: Surprise-Guided Token Reduction for Efficient Video Understanding with VLMs
why: SURGE retains unpredictable/high-surprise tokens and prunes predictable ones without training. The official abstract reports up to 7 times fewer tokens and 86–98 percent lower prefill cost with accuracy within ±1 point, a direct video-VLM efficiency result.

title: TableDART: Dynamic Adaptive Multi-Modal Routing for Table Understanding
why: The official abstract uses a 2.59M-parameter router to select text, image, or fusion paths dynamically, avoiding redundant processing and costly full-MLLM fine-tuning while improving accuracy. This is a direct efficiency contribution.

title: Tactic: Adaptive Sparse Attention with Clustering and Distribution Fitting for Long-Context LLMs
why: Calibration-free adaptive sparse attention using cumulative-attention targets plus clustering/distribution fitting; official ICLR paper reports up to 5.14x decode-attention and 1.51x end-to-end speedup.

title: Taming Hierarchical Image Coding Optimization: A Spectral Regularization Perspective
why: The official abstract reports 2.3x faster training and a 20.65% rate-distortion gain over VTM-22.0, with no inference overhead from the regularizers. This is a direct, quantified image-compression efficiency result.

title: TangoFlux: Super Fast and Faithful Text to Audio Generation with Flow Matching and Clap-Ranked Preference Optimization
topic: Fast text-to-audio generation with flow matching
why: The official abstract reports a 515M-parameter model generating up to 30 seconds of 44.1kHz audio in 3.7 seconds on an A40 GPU. This is a direct, quantified audio-generation latency result.

title: Task Tokens: A Flexible Approach to Adapting Behavior Foundation Models
topic: Parameter-efficient adaptation of robotic behavior foundation models
why: The official abstract reports up to 125 times fewer trainable parameters per task and up to 6 times faster convergence while leaving the behavior foundation model unchanged. This is a direct parameter- and training-efficient adaptation method for robot control.

title: Task-Aware Data Selection via Proxy-Label Enhanced Distribution Matching for LLM Finetuning
why: The official abstract selects only 10K examples from 300K while achieving competitive or better task-specific finetuning performance. This is direct data and training-cost reduction with first-party evidence.

title: Task-Related Token Compression in Multimodal Large Language Models from an Explainability Perspective
topic: Task-aware token compression for MLLM inference
why: The official abstract directly targets redundant multimodal tokens through task-related token compression. This is a core MLLM efficiency direction because reducing retained tokens can lower downstream attention and inference cost.

title: TD-MoE: Tensor Decomposition for MoE Models
topic: Cross-expert tensor decomposition for MoE compression
why: The official abstract reports almost lossless performance at 20% parameter reduction and stronger results than prior decomposition baselines at 40% and 60% compression on Qwen2-57B-A14B and Mixtral. This is a direct, quantified MoE compression contribution.

title: Tequila: Trapping-free Ternary Quantization for Large Language Models
topic: Ternary LLM quantization for hardware-efficient deployment
why: The official abstract targets LLM deployment and explains how ternary weights replace multiplications with hardware-efficient additions. The method directly addresses quantized LLM optimization and edge deployment, so it merits strong retention despite the abstract emphasizing optimization rather than a quantified serving benchmark.

title: Terminal Velocity Matching
topic: Single- and few-NFE flow matching for high-quality generation
why: The official abstract reports 3.29 FID at one NFE and 1.99 FID at four NFEs on ImageNet-256, with corresponding results at 512 resolution. This is a direct few-step generative-inference acceleration method.

title: Test-Time Accuracy-Cost Control in Neural Simulators via Recurrent-Depth
topic: Adaptive test-time compute and efficient neural simulation
why: The official abstract exposes a controllable accuracy-cost trade-off through recurrent depth and reports 13.5 percent less training memory and 44 percent fewer parameters in an architecture-compatible variant. It directly targets low-compute simulation and adaptive runtime cost.

title: Test-Time Efficient Pretrained Model Portfolios for Time Series Forecasting
why: The paper achieves competitive forecasting with much fewer parameters and reports ensembling/model selection as more compute-efficient than test-time fine-tuning. This is a direct model-size and test-time efficiency contribution

title: Test-Time Training Done Right
topic: Large-chunk test-time training for GPU utilization and long-context inference
why: The official abstract identifies below-5% FLOP utilization in prior TTT layers and proposes large chunks from 2K to 1M tokens, improving hardware utilization by orders of magnitude. This is a direct hardware-aware long-context inference contribution.

title: The Art of Scaling Reinforcement Learning Compute for LLMs
topic: Predictable and compute-efficient LLM RL scaling
why: The official abstract presents a 400,000-GPU-hour study, identifies recipe choices governing compute efficiency, and validates predictable scaling on a 100,000-GPU-hour run. This is a core RL-training efficiency contribution.

title: The Curious Case of In-Training Compression of State Space Models
why: The first-party abstract compresses SSM state dimensions during training, significantly accelerating optimization while preserving task-critical expressivity. This is a direct model-architecture and training-efficiency contribution.

title: The Gaussian-Head OFL Family: One-Shot Federated Learning from Client Global Statistics
why: GH-OFL reduces federated communication from multiple rounds to a single round and transmits only class statistics. This is a direct communication-efficiency contribution under non-IID settings

title: The Geometry of LLM Quantization: GPTQ as Babai's Nearest Plane Algorithm
topic: LLM quantization / GPTQ theory / low-bit inference kernels
why: DASLab reverse-census recall miss and ICLR 2026 canonical quantization work: proves GPTQ equivalence to Babai nearest-plane, derives error guarantees, introduces no-clipping PTQ variants, and supplies efficient GPU inference kernels.

title: The Markovian Thinker: Architecture-Agnostic Linear Scaling of Reasoning
why: The official abstract reports 40% faster reasoning and 70% less memory at equal performance, with linear compute and constant peak memory as reasoning length grows. This is a direct, quantified long-context inference and training-efficiency contribution.

title: THE PATH OF LEAST RESISTANCE: GUIDING LLM REASONING TRAJECTORIES WITH PREFIX CONSENSUS
topic: Prefix-consensus pruning for efficient LLM reasoning
why: The official abstract expands only promising reasoning prefixes and reports up to 60 percent lower token usage and 50 percent lower wall-clock latency while matching or exceeding self-consistency. This is a direct inference-time search optimization.

title: Thicker and Quicker: The Jumbo Token for Fast Plain Vision Transformers
topic: Jumbo-token architecture for faster vision transformers
why: The official abstract explicitly targets faster plain vision transformers with a jumbo-token design. This is a direct architecture-level acceleration contribution in the vision-model landscape.

title: ThinKV: Thought-Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Efficient Reasoning Models
why: Thought-adaptive hybrid KV quantization+eviction with a PagedAttention memory-reuse kernel; official ICLR paper reports near-lossless accuracy with <5% of original KV cache and up to 5.8x higher inference throughput.

title: Threading Keyframe with Narratives: MLLMs as Strong Long Video Comprehenders
topic: Efficient long-video MLLM perception via keyframe and narrative selection
why: The official abstract targets excessive visual-token/context cost and training burden for long videos, using relevance-diversity keyframe selection and temporally ordered narratives. This is a direct long-video perception efficiency contribution.

title: TileLang: Bridge Programmability and Performance in Modern Neural Kernels
topic: GPU kernel DSL and hardware-aware fused-kernel compilation
why: The official abstract reports up to 5x speedup over Triton on NVIDIA H100 and up to 6x on AMD GPUs while substantially reducing implementation code size.

title: Time Optimal Execution of Action Chunk Policies Beyond Demonstration Speed
topic: VLA action-chunk execution and robot-policy acceleration
why: The official abstract introduces RACE to align and re-time action chunks and reports up to 4 times faster execution while maintaining high success rates in simulation and real-world manipulation. This is a direct runtime acceleration for VLA/imitation policies.

title: Tina: Tiny Reasoning Models via LoRA
why: The official abstract reports competitive reasoning from a 1.5B model using LoRA-based reinforcement learning, with a best model costing about nine dollars and an estimated 260-fold cost reduction. This is a direct and quantified compute-efficiency contribution.

title: TINY BUT MIGHTY: A SOFTWARE-HARDWARE CO- DESIGN APPROACH FOR EFFICIENT MULTIMODAL IN- FERENCE ON BATTERY-POWERED SMALL DEVICES
topic: Heterogeneous accelerator co-design for on-device multimodal inference
why: The official abstract describes modular mapping and dynamic offloading across SoC accelerators and reports 42.3% lower energy consumption and 11.2% lower GPU memory usage on a battery-powered device.

title: TNT: Improving Chunkwise Training for Test-Time Memorization
topic: Hardware-utilization-aware training for test-time memorization models
why: The official abstract identifies slow training and low hardware utilization as bottlenecks in recurrent test-time-memorization models and introduces a two-stage training paradigm to decouple training efficiency from inference performance. This is a direct efficient-ML systems contribution.

title: Token-Efficient Long-Term Interest Sketching and Internalized Reasoning for LLM-based Recommendation
topic: Prompt compression and internalized reasoning for lower-cost LLM inference
why: The official abstract identifies long noisy histories and autoregressive rationale generation as practical inference-latency bottlenecks, then proposes compact token-bounded sketches and internalized reasoning. This is directly relevant to token/memory/inference efficiency.

title: TokMem: One-Token Procedural Memory for Large Language Models

title: LazyAttention: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Deferred Positional Encoding
topic: LLM serving / RAG / KV cache reuse / deferred positional encoding / attention kernels
why: ICML 2026 direct LLM-serving/KV-reuse systems work. LazyAttention defers positional encoding into attention kernels, enabling zero-copy position-agnostic KV reuse for RAG/ICL. It reports 1.37x lower TTFT and 1.40x higher inference throughput than Block-Attention under skewed document distributions while preserving output quality.

title: LC-QAT: Data-Efficient 2-Bit QAT for LLMs via Linear-Constrained Vector Quantization
topic: LLM quantization / 2-bit QAT / vector quantization / efficient deployment
why: ICML 2026 direct extreme-low-bit LLM deployment work. LC-QAT makes 2-bit vector-quantization QAT end-to-end differentiable via a linear-constrained codebook and achieves strong quality with only 0.1%-10% of conventional QAT training data, making 2-bit deployment substantially more practical.

title: LEAP: Zone-Aware MCTS for LLM Self-Speculative Decoding
topic: speculative decoding / self-speculative decoding / MCTS layer selection
why: ICML 2026 Poster; plug-and-play lossless self-speculative decoding using prefilling-derived redundancy and zone-aware MCTS to construct a per-instance lightweight draft model; reports 1.7x-2.0x inference speedup.

title: LearniBridge: Learnable Calibration of Feature Caching for Diffusion Models Acceleration
topic: video/image generation acceleration / diffusion transformer feature caching / low-rank cache calibration / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026. LearniBridge learns prompt-invariant low-rank calibration updates for cached Diffusion Transformer features using lightweight LoRA and only 3-5 training samples; reported acceleration reaches 5.87x on FLUX, 5.75x on HunyuanVideo, and 4.10x on Wan2.1 with improved VBench at the latter operating point.

title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / runtime memory / adaptive compute routing / performance-cost control
why: ICML 2026. BudgetMem performs runtime, query-aware memory construction with Low/Mid/High budget tiers and a lightweight RL router, explicitly optimizing performance-cost trade-offs across implementation, reasoning and model-capacity tiers on LoCoMo, LongMemEval and HotpotQA.

title: Learning to Evict from Key-Value Cache
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / learned eviction / reinforcement learning
why: ICML 2026 Apple work introducing KV Policy (KVP), lightweight per-head RL agents that learn future-utility-based eviction rankings from generation traces; outperforms heuristic eviction across RULER up to 128K and multi-turn dialogue while requiring no modification to the base LLM or extra inference passes.

title: Learning to Share: Selective Memory for Efficient Parallel Agentic Systems
topic: efficient agent systems / parallel agents / shared memory / computation reuse
why: ICML 2026. Introduces learned shared memory for parallel agent teams so useful intermediate steps can be reused across trajectories while controlling context growth, reducing redundant computation and runtime while matching or improving task quality on AssistantBench and GAIA; official UCF implementation verified.

title: Least-Loaded Expert Parallelism: Load Balancing An Imbalanced Mixture-of-Experts
topic: MoE systems / expert parallelism / distributed inference / load balancing
why: ICML 2026 system/algorithmic infrastructure work for imbalanced MoE expert parallelism. LLEP dynamically reroutes excess tokens together with expert parameters to underutilized devices; authors report up to 5x speedup and 4x lower peak memory versus standard EP, including about 1.9x faster full-model inference for gpt-oss-120b.

title: Less Is More: Training-Free Sparse Attention with Global Locality for Efficient Reasoning
topic: efficient reasoning / sparse attention / KV-cache decoding
why: ICML 2026; training-free cross-head unified sparse attention for long reasoning. Official author/Princeton pages confirm acceptance; reports lossless AIME-24 accuracy with up to 87.5% fewer attended tokens and about 1.13x end-to-end generation speedup.

title: Less Token, More Signal: MoE Expert Pruning via Critical Token Selection
topic: MoE systems / expert pruning / memory-efficient inference
why: ICML 2026 Poster. STEP uses critical-token-guided expert importance with loss-aware evaluation and lightweight knowledge preservation; on Qwen3-30B with 50% expert sparsity it nearly halves memory, improves throughput by about 1.5x, and completes pruning in under 10 minutes.

title: LFQ: Logit-aware Final-block Quantization for Boosting the Generation Quality of Low-Bit Quantized LLMs
topic: LLM quantization / PTQ / long-form generation quality
why: ICML 2026 direct low-bit LLM PTQ paper addressing long-generation quality degradation through logit-aware final-block quantization; complements block-wise PTQ and reasoning-focused deployment routes.

title: LiftQuant: Continuous Bit-Width Control for Pareto-Optimal LLM Deployment
topic: quantization / fractional bit-width / memory-constrained LLM deployment
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Continuous effective bit-width enables Pareto-optimal LLM fitting under exact GPU memory budgets; a 70B model can be fit at ~2.4 bits with a hardware-friendly decoding path.

title: Light Forcing: Accelerating Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Sparse Attention
topic: video generation acceleration / autoregressive video / sparse attention / kernels
why: ICML 2026 direct video-generation efficiency work; chunk-aware hierarchical sparse attention gives ~1.2-1.3x E2E alone and ~2-3x with deployment optimizations; official repository provides sparse kernels and quantized deployment paths.

title: LightningRL: Breaking the Accuracy-Parallelism Trade-off of Block-wise dLLMs via Reinforcement Learning
topic: diffusion LLM / parallel decoding / RL post-training / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 direct dLLM acceleration; RL optimizes speed-quality Pareto frontier and the official implementation reports 336 TPS on H100, ~3.2x faster than SDAR while maintaining high accuracy.

title: LiME: Lightweight Mixture of Experts for Efficient Multimodal Multi-task Learning
topic: multimodal efficiency / lightweight MoE / parameter-efficient fine-tuning / adaptive routing
why: ICML 2026 multimodal-efficiency work. LiME replaces per-expert adapter replication with shared PEFT plus lightweight expert modulation and zero-parameter routing, using up to 4x fewer trainable parameters and up to 29% faster training than MoE-PEFT baselines.

title: LiMuon: Light and Fast Muon Optimizer for Large Models
topic: LLM training efficiency / memory-efficient optimizer / Muon
why: ICML 2026; lowers Muon optimizer memory with randomized SVD and improves stochastic sample complexity via variance reduction, with experiments on Mamba-130M, Qwen2.5-0.5B and ViT showing practical training-efficiency gains.

title: LK Losses: Direct Acceptance Rate Optimization for Speculative Decoding
topic: speculative decoding / draft-model training / acceptance optimization
why: ICML 2026. Replaces KL-proxy draft training with acceptance-aligned LK objectives; across four draft architectures and six target models (8B-685B), improves average acceptance length by up to about 8-10% with no inference overhead and integrates directly into existing speculator training pipelines.

title: Locally Coherent Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
topic: diffusion language model / parallel decoding / local autoregressive decoding / efficient code generation / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-track paper from IBM Research/ETH Zurich. CoDiLA combines global diffusion-LM parallel generation with a compact local autoregressive decoder operating on diffusion latents, preserving sub-linear generation latency while repairing local syntactic dependencies that otherwise break parallel decoding. It establishes an improved accuracy-speed Pareto frontier for code generation and is a direct diffusion-LM parallel-decoding efficiency work.

title: LoKiFormer: Locality-aware Attention with Decoupled Knowledge Memory for Efficient Large Language Model Pretraining
topic: LLM pretraining efficiency / efficient attention / explicit knowledge memory
why: ICML 2026; introduces Local Fusion Attention plus a decoupled parametric Knowledge Memory Module to reduce redundant local modeling and separate knowledge storage from computation; reports 1.33x faster pretraining convergence than Transformer baselines.

title: Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
topic: efficient attention / long-context LLM inference / on-device inference
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight; DHSA predicts content-dependent sparse attention online with variable-length hierarchical routing and memory-efficient GPU/CPU backends; reports up to 10x prefill speedup at 128K and enables 100K context on a single 24GB GPU while preserving near-dense accuracy.

title: LoSA: Locality Aware Sparse Attention for Block-Wise Diffusion Language Models
topic: efficient attention / diffusion language model acceleration / KV reuse / sparse attention / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026. Addresses KV Inflation in block-wise diffusion language models by reusing cached prefix-attention for stable tokens and applying sparse attention only to active tokens. It reports 1.54x lower attention density and up to 4.14x attention speedup on RTX A6000 while preserving near-dense accuracy.

title: LRAgent: Efficient KV Cache Sharing for Multi-LoRA LLM Agents
topic: KV cache sharing / multi-LoRA agent serving / Flash-LoRA-Attention
why: Multi-LoRA agent serving framework that decomposes KV cache into a shared base component plus low-rank adapter-dependent cache; reports up to 2.46x throughput, 4.44x TTFT reduction and about 3x KV-cache memory reduction while preserving accuracy.

title: LSGQuant: Layer-Sensitivity Guided Quantization for One-Step Diffusion Real-World Video Super-Resolution
topic: quantization / video generation acceleration / diffusion transformer / low-bit inference
why: ICML 2026 direct diffusion/video quantization work. Layer-sensitivity guided PTQ combines dynamic-range-aware activation quantization, variance-oriented layer training, and quantization-aware optimization to compress one-step DiT video super-resolution while preserving near-full-precision quality; author publication page and ICML listing confirm venue, and official author repository is verified.

title: LUGS: Latent-aware Guidance for Efficient Unmasking in Diffusion Large Language Models
topic: diffusion language model acceleration / efficient decoding / unmasking policy / latent guidance
why: ICML 2026 poster. Direct dLLM inference-efficiency work: uses latent hidden-state guidance to improve unmasking decisions beyond local confidence/entropy heuristics, targeting better quality-efficiency trade-offs in parallel diffusion decoding.

title: M+Adam: Low-Precision Training via Additive-Multiplicative Optimization
topic: low-precision training / FP8 FP4 / optimizer / memory efficiency
why: ICML 2026. Combines additive and multiplicative updates to train directly with BF16, FP8, and FP4 master weights without higher-precision copies; improves low-precision LLaMA-style pretraining across model scales and budgets.

title: ManifoldKV: Training-Free KV Cache Compression via Euclidean Outlier Detection
topic: KV cache compression / training-free eviction / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026 training-free KV compression using Euclidean outlier detection; improves multi-key retrieval robustness and restores 64K-context performance with windowed scoring while requiring minimal implementation changes.

title: MAPS: Memory-Aware Predictive Scheduling Framework for Large Language Model Serving
topic: LLM serving / disaggregated inference / predictive scheduling / memory-aware scheduling
why: ICML 2026 Poster; device-assisted speculative output-length prediction overlapped with cloud prefilling plus uncertainty-calibrated hierarchical scheduling for memory-bound disaggregated decode; reports 42.6% lower mean end-to-end latency and up to 84.8% lower tail latency versus three serving baselines.

title: MedCoG: Maximizing LLM Inference Density in Medical Reasoning via Meta-Cognitive Regulation
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / inference-time compute allocation / adaptive knowledge use
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. Meta-cognitive regulation avoids indiscriminate inference scaling by adaptively deciding when and how to use procedural, episodic, and factual knowledge; reports roughly 5.5x inference density on difficult medical reasoning benchmarks.

title: MemOCR: Layout-Aware Visual Memory for Efficient Long-Horizon Reasoning
topic: efficient reasoning / agent memory / multimodal memory compression / long-horizon context efficiency
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper confirmed by official/author sources and Meituan repository. MemOCR compresses growing interaction histories into adaptive visual layouts and reports about 8x token-efficiency gain under extreme budgets, making it a canonical context/memory-efficiency route for long-horizon agents.

title: Memory-Efficient LLM Pretraining via Minimalist Optimizer Design
topic: distributed training / memory-efficient LLM pretraining / optimizer-state reduction
why: ICML 2026 memory-efficient LLM pretraining work. SCALE combines column-wise gradient normalization with first-order momentum only on the output layer, matching or exceeding Adam while using only about 35-45% of total memory across 60M-1B models and outperforming memory-efficient baselines such as GaLore/Fira/APOLLO; the official OptimAI-Lab repository provides the implementation.

title: Memory-Efficient LLM Training with Dynamic Sparsity: From Stability to Practical Scaling
topic: LLM training efficiency / dynamic sparsity / memory-efficient optimization
why: ICML 2026; Sparse Memory-Efficient Training stabilizes dynamic sparse LLM pretraining with optimizer warm-up and density-aware learning-rate scaling while storing gradients and optimizer states only for active parameters, making sparse pretraining materially memory-efficient.

title: Mining Tensor/Neuron-Level Sparsity to Maximize Mixture-of-Experts Potential in Post-Training and Inference
topic: MoE systems / post-training sparsity / token-expert dropping / expert partition / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper, with the same author set as the earlier arXiv title DualSparse-MoE. It exploits tensor-level and neuron-level sparsity after pretraining via expert partitioning, threshold-based token-expert dropping, partial partition/reconstruction, and load-imbalance-aware execution. Reported inference-only results reach up to 1.41x MoE speedup with under 0.5% accuracy loss, making it a direct MoE deployment-efficiency canonical.

title: MixFP4: Enhancing NVFP4 with Adaptive FP4/INT4 Block Representations
topic: quantization / FP4-INT4 micro-format / Tensor Core co-design / LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 poster. MixFP4 extends NVFP4 with per-block E2M1/E1M2 selection while reusing the FP8 block-scale sign bit for zero-extra-metadata format tagging and a unified internal compute representation; reports improved 4-bit robustness with only 3.1% area and 1.5% power overhead in the proposed Tensor Core support.

title: MixQuant: Pushing the Limits of Block Rotations in Post-Training Quantization
topic: quantization / post-training quantization / block Hadamard rotation / low-bit LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 direct low-bit PTQ work. MixQuant/PeRQ analyzes the limits of block Hadamard rotations and calibrates permutation-based activation-mass redistribution before rotation, then folds permutations into model weights so deployment adds no inference overhead; experiments recover up to about 90% of full-vector-rotation perplexity for INT4 Llama3-1B at block size 16.

title: Mixture of Distributions Matters: Dynamic Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion Transformers
topic: video generation acceleration / diffusion / dynamic sparse attention
why: ICML 2026 video-DiT efficiency work. MOD-DiT models evolving attention sparsity with a mixture-of-distributions approximation plus online block masking, avoiding repeated expensive sparsity sampling while preserving generation quality and accelerating video diffusion attention.

title: Model-Preserving Adaptive Rounding
topic: quantization / LLM PTQ / adaptive rounding / model-preserving compression
why: ICML 2026 Cornell RelaxML quantization paper introducing YAQA, an adaptive-rounding PTQ method using full-model/Kronecker-factored Hessian approximations rather than layer-local activation error. Primary arXiv reports about 30% lower KL divergence to the original model across models/quantizers with no inference overhead; official Christopher De Sa publication page lists it as ICML 2026.

title: MoSE: Mixture of Slimmable Experts for Efficient and Adaptive Language Models
topic: MoE / conditional computation / slimmable experts / adaptive inference FLOPs
why: ICML 2026 efficient-MoE work. MoSE makes each expert slimmable, allowing runtime control over both which experts execute and how much of each expert executes. It shifts the accuracy-compute Pareto frontier toward lower inference FLOPs and supports budget-aware runtime width selection.

title: MoshiRAG: Asynchronous Knowledge Retrieval for Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
topic: multimodal serving / full-duplex speech LM / asynchronous RAG / real-time inference
why: ICML 2026 real-time multimodal serving work. MoshiRAG keeps a compact full-duplex speech-language interface while asynchronously retrieving stronger knowledge sources during the natural response gap, improving factuality without sacrificing real-time interactivity; the official implementation includes production-oriented Rust inference code.

title: Motion-Aware Caching for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
topic: autoregressive video generation / cache reuse / diffusion acceleration
why: ICML 2026. MotionCache uses token-level motion-aware cache reuse instead of coarse chunk skipping; reports 6.28x on SkyReels-V2 and 1.64x on MAGI-1 with very small quality loss.

title: Multi-Head LatentMoE and Head Parallel: Communication-Efficient and Deterministic MoE Parallelism
topic: MoE systems / distributed training / communication-efficient parallelism / deterministic routing / IO-aware execution
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. Multi-Head LatentMoE with Head Parallel achieves O(1) communication cost with respect to activated experts, fully balanced deterministic traffic, and IO-aware routing/expert computation; compared with MoE expert parallelism it reports up to 1.61x faster training at identical performance.

title: Multipole Semantic Attention: A Fast Approximation of Softmax Attention for Pretraining
topic: efficient attention / long-context pretraining / attention approximation
why: ICML 2026. Semantic clustering plus multipole expansions gives subquadratic/drop-in attention; reports 3x isolated-layer speedup over cuDNN FlashAttention at 8k and material end-to-end long-context pretraining runtime reductions with small loss degradation.

title: MVR-cache: Optimizing Semantic Caching via Multi-Vector Retrieval and Learned Prompt Segmentation
topic: LLM serving / semantic cache / response reuse / retrieval / inference cost reduction
why: ICML 2026 semantic-caching system for LLM serving. MVR-cache learns prompt segmentation and uses multi-vector retrieval/MaxSim to improve semantically safe response-cache reuse; experiments report up to 37% higher cache hit rate at the same correctness guarantee, directly reducing repeated LLM inference cost and latency.

title: NanoFLUX: Distillation-Driven Compression of Large Text-to-Image Generation Models for Mobile Devices
topic: image generation acceleration / flow matching / model compression / mobile edge AI / distillation
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads lists NanoFLUX as a main-conference paper. NanoFLUX progressively compresses FLUX.1-Schnell from a 17B teacher to a 2.4B mobile text-to-image model using DiT pruning, token downsampling, and text-encoder distillation, reporting 512x512 generation in about 2.5 seconds on a mobile device.

title: NanoQuant: Efficient Sub-1-Bit Quantization of Large Language Models
topic: quantization / sub-1-bit PTQ / custom kernels / consumer-GPU deployment
why: ICML 2026. Sub-1-bit post-training quantization with custom low-bit kernels; reports extreme model-memory compression and practical consumer-GPU deployment while preserving useful accuracy.

title: NanoSpec: Accelerating Speculative Decoding using Minimalist In-Context Vocabularies
topic: speculative decoding / active-vocabulary pruning / GPU runtime
why: ICML 2026. Training-free speculative-decoding co-design that restricts draft computation to a small dynamic in-context vocabulary and combines asynchronous gathering/GPU-resident state to reduce draft cost and improve end-to-end speed.

title: Native Parallel Reasoner: Reasoning in Parallelism via Self-Distilled Reinforcement Learning
topic: efficient reasoning / parallel reasoning / SGLang runtime / reinforcement learning / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. NPR trains models to reason with genuine parallel execution rather than serial autoregressive traces; its NPR Engine refactors SGLang memory/flow control for parallel RL and inference, reporting up to 4.6x inference acceleration across reasoning benchmarks.

title: NeUQI: Near-Optimal Uniform Quantization Parameter Initialization for Low-Bit LLMs
topic: LLM quantization / low-bit PTQ / uniform quantization / parameter initialization / consumer-GPU deployment
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper confirmed by the senior-author publication list. NeUQI replaces suboptimal Min-Max initialization with efficient near-optimal initialization for uniform low-bit PTQ and is designed to improve practical memory/decoding efficiency on consumer-grade hardware.

title: No Retraining at Edge: Efficient Resource-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantization via Federated Supernet Learning
topic: edge AI / mixed-precision quantization / federated supernet / resource-adaptive deployment
why: ICML 2026 Poster. DFMPQ trains a weight-sharing mixed-precision federated supernet once, then derives resource-aware quantized subnets for changing edge constraints without retraining; directly targets heterogeneous edge deployment cost.

title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable
topic: distributed LLM training / optimizer / FSDP2 / training efficiency
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Neuron-wise normalized Muon with a distributed FSDP2 implementation; Microsoft reports 21.74% better training efficiency than Adam and 11.31% improvement over Muon on 1.1B pretraining with comparable memory footprint.

title: Not All Prefills Are Equal: PPD Disaggregation for Multi-turn LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / prefill-decode disaggregation / multi-turn KV reuse
why: ICML 2026; dynamic PPD routing reuses cached KV for Turn 2+ append-prefill on decode nodes and reports about 68% lower Turn 2+ TTFT while controlling TPOT and KV-transfer congestion.

title: OBCache: Optimal Brain KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / output-aware eviction / pruning
why: ICML 2026. Formulates KV eviction as structured pruning using output-aware Optimal-Brain-Damage saliency; plug-and-play with H2O/TOVA/SnapKV/AdaKV and consistently improves long-context eviction quality. Official code is built on NVIDIA KVPress.

title: On Effectiveness and Efficiency of Agentic Tool-calling and RL Training
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / tool calling / RL training efficiency / rollout efficiency / wall-clock acceleration
why: ICML 2026. Identifies wasted rollout compute from zero-learning-signal prompts and high policy-update cost in RL-based tool-calling training, then introduces complementary techniques that substantially accelerate wall-clock training without degrading tool-calling performance; also audits evaluation-pipeline instability.

title: On Efficient Scaling of GNNs via IO-Aware Layers Implementations
topic: GPU kernel / graph neural network systems / IO-aware layers / sparse attention / SpMM / hardware-efficient training and inference
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Develops IO-aware GPU kernels for SpMM, reductions, GATv2 and Graph Transformer layers; reports up to 8.5x GATv2 speedup, 7.3x Tensor-Core Graph-Transformer speedup on locally dense graphs, and up to 76x peak-memory reduction, with drop-in implementations.

title: Online Linear Programming for Multi-Objective Routing in LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / request routing / SLO optimization / KV-cache-aware scheduling
why: ICML 2026 LLM-serving routing framework formulated as online linear programming under batch-size and KV-cache constraints, with warm-started dual updates for millisecond decisions and improved latency/TTFT/throughput/tail metrics in Vidur.

title: Optimal Self-Consistency for Efficient Reasoning with Large Language Models
topic: efficient reasoning / test-time scaling / adaptive sampling / self-consistency
why: ICML 2026. Blend-ASC dynamically allocates self-consistency samples under arbitrary budgets and uses 6.8x fewer samples than vanilla self-consistency on average while maintaining reasoning performance.

title: OSAQ: Outlier Self-Absorption for Accurate Low-bit LLM Quantization
topic: LLM quantization / weight-only low-bit PTQ / outlier suppression
why: ICML 2026. Closed-form Hessian-null-space additive transformation suppresses weight outliers offline with no inference overhead; substantially improves 2-bit GPTQ perplexity.

title: OServe: Accelerating LLM Serving via Spatial-Temporal Workload Orchestration
ParisKV: Fast and Drift-Robust KV-Cache Retrieval for Long-Context LLMs
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / GPU retrieval / CPU offload
why: GPU-native drift-robust KV-cache retrieval with collision-based candidate selection, 4-bit reranking and UVA CPU offload; reports up to 2.8x higher throughput in the full-attention runnable range and 17x/44x lower decode latency than MagicPIG/PQCache at million-token scale. Official ICML 2026 poster/slides and arXiv identity verified.

title: PatternKV: Flattening KV Representation Expands Quantization Headroom
topic: KV cache / quantization / long-context inference / test-time scaling
why: ICML 2026 direct KV-cache quantization work. Pattern-aligned residual quantization flattens native KV distributions before low-bit coding; reports near-lossless 4-bit behavior, stronger 2-bit quality, about 10% average test-time-scaling accuracy gain, 1.4x throughput, and 1.25x larger supported batches.

title: PETS: A Principled Framework Towards Optimal Trajectory Allocation for Efficient Test-Time Self-Consistency
topic: efficient reasoning / test-time scaling / adaptive trajectory allocation
why: ICML 2026; principled offline/online allocation of reasoning trajectories under a sampling budget; reports up to 75% lower offline and 55% lower online sampling budget for the same self-consistency target.

title: PinTok: Tokenizers Deserve Dedicated Pinned CPU-Compute and Memory
topic: LLM serving / tokenizer runtime / CPU pinning / latency-sensitive inference
why: ICML 2026; treats tokenization as a first-class serving bottleneck and reduces OS scheduling, context-switch, memory-placement, and packet-copy overhead via dedicated pinned CPU compute and memory.

title: PipeSD: An Efficient Cloud-Edge Collaborative Pipeline Inference Framework with Speculative Decoding
topic: cloud-edge LLM inference / speculative decoding / pipeline scheduling
why: ICML 2026; real cloud-edge testbed combining token-batch pipelining and adaptive verification triggering; reports 1.16x-2.16x speedup and 14.3%-25.3% energy reduction.

title: Plan for Speed: Dilated Scheduling for Masked Diffusion Language Models
topic: diffusion language model / parallel decoding / inference-only scheduling / generation acceleration
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads inventory paper. Proposes an inference-only dilated unmasking scheduler that parallelizes masked-diffusion generation without retraining and explicitly targets the speed-quality frontier.

title: PLASH: Provably Linear-Time Attention with Selective Higher-Order Feature Sketching
topic: efficient attention / long-context / linear-time attention / feature sketching
why: ICML 2026 official poster. Compresses keys/values into learned prototypes with polynomial feature enrichment and provides linear-time runtime bounds, directly targeting long-context training and inference cost.

title: PLoRA: Efficient Concurrent LoRA Training for Large Language Models
topic: LLM training systems / LoRA / GPU utilization / concurrent training / custom kernels
why: ICML 2026 main-conference systems paper confirmed by author publication pages and the official inventory. Orchestrates concurrent LoRA fine-tuning jobs and custom GPU kernels, reporting up to 12.8x training throughput and 7.52x shorter makespan.

title: POET-X: Memory-efficient LLM Training by Scaling Orthogonal Transformation
topic: distributed LLM training / memory-efficient optimizer / Triton kernels
why: ICML 2026 Oral. Scalable orthogonal-equivalence training with input-centric reconstruction, structured/blockwise transforms and kernel engineering; enables billion-parameter pretraining on a single H100 where AdamW OOMs and materially improves memory/throughput over original POET.

title: PRAC: Principal-Random Subspace for LLM Activation Compression and Memory-Efficient Training
topic: distributed training / activation compression / memory-efficient LLM training
why: ICML 2026 direct memory-efficient LLM training work. PRAC decomposes activations into principal and random subspaces, yields an unbiased low-variance gradient estimator, and reports up to 36% total memory reduction with negligible quality loss. ICML Downloads and senior-author publication page confirm acceptance.

title: Predicting Future Utility: Global Combinatorial Optimization for Task-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction
topic: KV cache compression / head-wise budget allocation / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026 LU-KV; long-horizon marginal-utility optimization for head-wise KV budget allocation, reporting 80% KV-cache reduction with minimal degradation while reducing latency and GPU memory footprint.

title: Predictive Prefetching for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
topic: RAG serving / asynchronous retrieval / predictive prefetching / latency reduction
why: ICML 2026 RAG-serving acceleration; predicts when and what to retrieve before uncertainty peaks, reporting up to 43.5% lower end-to-end latency and 62.4% TTFT improvement while preserving answer quality.

title: Prefix-Cache-Aware Data Reordering for LLM-Augmented Database Analytics
topic: LLM serving / prefix KV-cache reuse / prompt-data layout / database analytics
why: ICML 2026 data-systems/LLM-serving work (SOLO) that reorders relational rows/columns to maximize reusable prompt prefixes; reports up to 90.3% higher prefill throughput and up to 242x lower planning overhead.

title: Preserve-Then-Quantize: Balancing Rank Budgets for Quantization Error Reconstruction in LLMs

why: ICML 2026 official Downloads lists Preserve-Then-Quantize. title: PRIM: Cooperative Dynamic Token Compression for Efficient Large Multimodal Models

why: ICML 2026 official Downloads and the BUPT PESI official lab page confirm PRIM. It performs cooperative audio-video token compression across encoders and the language model using text-conditioned fusion, attention/frequency-aware pruning, and task-adaptive retention, reducing long-form multimodal inference FLOPs/latency while preserving accuracy.

title: Principled SVD-based Delta Compression via Quantization Error Minimization
topic: quantization / delta-model compression / multi-tenant LLM serving / storage efficiency / mixed precision
why: ICML 2026 Poster. PrinMix formulates SVD delta quantization as bit-budget-constrained optimization with reconstruction target correction, targeting storage and GPU-memory overhead of many fine-tuned LLM variants; reported results include over 6x storage savings and substantial accuracy gains over prior delta-compression baselines.

title: Prism-MoE: Efficient Dense-to-MoE Conversion for Visual Autoregressive Generation
topic: MoE systems / visual autoregressive generation / sparse activation / efficient model conversion
why: ICML 2026 Poster. Prism-MoE converts pretrained dense visual autoregressive generators into sparse MoE models using trajectory-consistent initialization and lightweight confidence-adaptive fine-tuning; reports dense-like generation quality with 37.5% active parameters and less than 10% of standard training budget.

title: Prism: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Hierarchical Search and Self-Verification for Discrete Diffusion Language Models
topic: efficient reasoning / diffusion language models / test-time scaling
why: ICML 2026 efficient test-time scaling for dLLMs; hierarchical trajectory search, partial remasking and self-verification match Best-of-N quality with substantially fewer function evaluations.

title: Prism: Spectral-Aware Block-Sparse Attention
topic: efficient attention / long-context prefill / Triton kernels
why: ICML 2026; training-free spectral-aware block-sparse attention with custom Triton kernels, reporting up to 5.1x speedup at 128K context with negligible accuracy loss.

title: Proact-VL: A Proactive VideoLLM for Real-Time AI Companions
